VBO:0200361.summary: Quiet and self-possessed, Chow Chows tend to be loyal to familiar people yet reserved when meeting strangers. They guarded homes and accompanied hunts in China long before the breed reached Britain. That measured manner helps explain why their watchfulness can be easy to underestimate.
VBO:0200361.shortDescription: Quiet and self-possessed, the Chow Chow is loyal to familiar people but reserved with strangers, reflecting a long guarding history.

VBO:0200363.summary: Chukotka Sled Dog is a dog breed or regional type associated with Russia.

VBO:0200364.summary: The Cimarrón Uruguayo tends to be balanced, intelligent and courageous, traits later valued for guarding estates and working cattle. Its ancestors descended from dogs introduced to Uruguay during the colonial era, then survived as free-ranging animals. The exact early mix is uncertain, but the move from survival to purposeful stock work is central to its story.
VBO:0200364.shortDescription: Balanced and courageous, the Cimarrón Uruguayo moved from free-ranging survival to purposeful estate guarding and cattle work.
VBO:0200364.historicalRoots: Uruguayan cattle and estate guardian descended from introduced colonial dogs.

VBO:0200365.summary: The Cirneco dell'Etna can be resolute and strong-willed in a chase, yet affectionate with familiar people. On Sicily's rocky slopes it uses scent to find wild rabbit in crevices, a precise hunting skill with deep local roots; dogs like it appear on ancient coins from the island.
VBO:0200365.shortDescription: Resolute in pursuit yet affectionate with familiar people, the Cirneco dell'Etna uses scent to find rabbits in Sicily's rocky crevices.

VBO:0200366.summary: Steady and kindly, the Clumber Spaniel often works with more deliberation than other spaniels. It flushes game quietly through cover, trusting an excellent nose rather than speed, and can be somewhat reserved when first meeting people. The breed’s history is tied to Clumber Park in Nottinghamshire; patience is part of both its work and its manner.
VBO:0200366.shortDescription: Steady and kindly, the Clumber Spaniel works quietly through cover, relying on its nose and patient pace more than speed.
VBO:0200366.historicalRoots: British flushing spaniel associated with Clumber Park.

VBO:0200372.summary: Cocker Spaniel is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200373.summary: Cocker Spaniel, A.S.C.O.B is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200374.summary: Cocker Spaniel, Parti-Colour is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200375.summary: Collie is a dog breed or regional type associated with United Kingdom.

VBO:0200376.summary: Friendly and active, Rough Collies often pair an easy sociability with a watchful interest in what is happening around them. They descend from the working dogs of Scottish shepherds, and many retain the ability to herd when given the chance. Rough and Smooth Collies share that recent ancestry despite their very different coats.
VBO:0200376.shortDescription: Friendly and active, the Rough Collie pairs sociability with watchfulness; its Scottish shepherd roots still show in herding ability.
VBO:0200376.historicalRoots: Scottish shepherding collie, refined in Great Britain.

VBO:0200377.summary: Outgoing and quick to learn, Smooth Collies tend to form close bonds with their families and respond well to patient, reward-based training. They may bark at an unfamiliar sound but usually settle when a visitor is welcomed, showing the alert yet steady manner valued in this British sheepdog.
VBO:0200377.shortDescription: Outgoing and quick to learn, the Smooth Collie bonds closely with family and may alert to unfamiliar sounds before settling.

VBO:0200378.summary: Colombian Fino Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200379.summary: Combai is a dog breed or regional type associated with India.

VBO:0200380.summary: Attentive, self-confident and friendly, the Continental Bulldog developed in Switzerland as an active companion. English Bulldog and Old English Bulldog crosses shaped a breed that kept recognizable bulldog character while placing more emphasis on athletic movement.
VBO:0200380.shortDescription: Attentive, self-confident and friendly, this Swiss bulldog was developed as an active companion.
VBO:0200380.historicalRoots: Swiss breed developed from English Bulldog and Old English Bulldog crosses as a medium-sized, active bull-type dog.

VBO:0200381.summary: Continental Toy Spaniel is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200382.summary: Lively and engaging, the Papillon retains the spirit of a little spaniel beneath its delicate look. Continental Toy Spaniels appear in European paintings for centuries; the erect-eared Papillon variety became fashionable later than its drop-eared relative.
VBO:0200382.shortDescription: Lively and engaging, the erect-eared Papillon keeps a little spaniel’s alert curiosity and companion spirit.
VBO:0200382.historicalRoots: French and Belgian Continental Toy Spaniel lineage depicted in European Renaissance art; erect-ear Papillon developed later than drop-ear Phalène.

VBO:0200383.summary: Lively and companionable, the Phalène shares the Continental Toy Spaniel’s small, alert presence with the Papillon. Its history reaches back to the drop-eared toy spaniels portrayed in European art before the erect-eared variety became familiar. The name means “moth,” referring to the softly hanging ears.
VBO:0200383.shortDescription: Lively and companionable, this toy spaniel shares a long European companion history with its erect-eared relative.

VBO:0200384.summary: Coonhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200385.summary: Cordoba Fighting Dog is a historical dog breed or type associated with Argentina.

VBO:0200387.summary: Corgi Pug is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0200389.summary: Cotons de Tulear are cheerful, sociable companions who tend to enjoy the company of both people and other dogs. Their adaptable, even-tempered character is central to the breed’s identity. From Madagascar, they became established companions in France before spreading more widely.
VBO:0200389.shortDescription: Cheerful and sociable, the Coton de Tulear enjoys people and other dogs; its even-tempered companion history began in Madagascar.
VBO:0200389.historicalRoots: Companion breed associated with Madagascar and the port of Tulear/Toliara.

VBO:0200390.summary: Coydog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200391.summary: The Cretan Hound tends to be gentle and affectionate with its people, yet persistent and daring on a hare trail. It works by both sight and scent across rocky ground, often hunting alone or in a pair. The breed standard notes a distinctive, fairly quiet voice when the dog sights or pursues quarry.
VBO:0200391.shortDescription: Gentle with its people and persistent on rocky hare trails, the Cretan Hound hunts by both sight and scent.

VBO:0200392.summary: The Croatian Sheepdog tends to be devoted, lively and level-headed, staying interested in its surroundings without becoming nervous. It has long worked livestock in eastern Slavonia, using quick reactions and sustained attention around moving animals. Its quick responses help it turn and redirect livestock as the flock moves.
VBO:0200392.shortDescription: Devoted and lively without nervousness, the Croatian Sheepdog reacts quickly to turn and redirect moving livestock.
VBO:0200392.historicalRoots: Eastern Slavonian livestock herder; systematic breeding from 1935.

VBO:0200394.summary: Cumberland Sheepdog is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200395.summary: Cur is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200396.summary: Curly Coated Murray River Retriever is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200397.summary: The Curly Coated Retriever is often steady, confident and friendly with people it knows, though it may seem reserved at first. Bred for British game retrieval, it can work independently through difficult cover; that self-reliant streak distinguishes its style from a more exuberant retriever's.
VBO:0200397.shortDescription: Steady and confident with familiar people, the Curly Coated Retriever works independently through difficult cover to retrieve game.

VBO:0200398.summary: The Cursinu can be calm at home yet lively at work, strongly attached to its person while remaining wary of strangers. Corsican farmers used it to bring back stray free-ranging animals rather than drive an entire herd; later the same adaptable dog found a place in scent hunting through the island's rough cover.
VBO:0200398.shortDescription: Calm at home and lively in action, this Corsican worker once brought strays back to the herd.
VBO:0200398.historicalRoots: Corsican stock work and later scent-hunting heritage.

VBO:0200399.summary: Cyprus Poodle is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0200400.summary: Cyprus Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200401.summary: Czechoslovakian Shepherd Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200402.summary: Quick to react and deeply loyal to familiar people, the Czechoslovakian Wolfdog is also noted for stamina and caution around strangers. It began in a 1955 Czechoslovakian working experiment crossing German Shepherd Dogs with Carpathian wolves.
VBO:0200402.shortDescription: Quick to react and loyal to familiar people, the Czechoslovakian Wolfdog has stamina and caution around strangers.
VBO:0200402.interestingFact: Both male-dog-to-female-wolf and male-wolf-to-female-dog matings were used in the original experiment.
VBO:0200402.historicalRoots: Czechoslovakian working breed founded in 1955 wolf-dog crosses.

VBO:0200403.summary: Czechoslovakian Wolfhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200404.summary: Czesky Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200405.summary: Dachsbracke is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200406.summary: Dachshunds combine a friendly, even-tempered side with the persistence of a serious hunter. They follow scent with determination, and their traditional work extends well beyond going underground: they also flush game, follow a trail while calling, and track wounded animals above ground. The familiar household companion still carries a remarkably varied hunting résumé.
VBO:0200406.shortDescription: Friendly yet persistent on a trail, the Dachshund tracks, flushes game and follows quarry both above and below ground.
VBO:0200406.historicalRoots: German hunting dog developed for work below ground.

VBO:0200407.summary: Dachshund, Long-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200408.summary: Dachshund, Miniature is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200409.summary: Dachshund, Miniature Long-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200410.summary: Dachshund, Miniature Smooth-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200411.summary: Dachshund, Miniature Wire-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200413.summary: Dachshund, Rabbit is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200414.summary: Dachshund, Rabbit Long-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200415.summary: Dachshund, Rabbit Smooth-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200416.summary: Dachshund, Rabbit Wire-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200417.summary: Dachshund, Smooth-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200418.summary: Dachshund, Standard is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200419.summary: Dachshund, Standard Long-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200420.summary: Dachshund, Standard Smooth-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200421.summary: Dachshund, Standard Wire-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200422.summary: Dachshund, Teckel is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200423.summary: Dachshund, Wire-Haired is a variety of Dachshund.

VBO:0200424.summary: Dakotah Shepherd Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200425.summary: Dalbo Dog is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200427.summary: The Dalmatian has a lively, independent streak, a marked hunting instinct and an affinity for water and outdoor activity. Its association with carriages grew alongside these active tendencies. Spotted dogs appear in Croatian regional art and church records from the seventeenth century, tying the breed’s name and history to Dalmatia.
VBO:0200427.shortDescription: Lively and independent, the Dalmatian has a marked hunting instinct and an affinity for water and outdoor activity.
VBO:0200427.historicalRoots: Croatian Dalmatian-region hound with later coach-dog history.

VBO:0200428.summary: Dalmatian Spaniel is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0200429.summary: The Dandie Dinmont Terrier is a determined, persistent worker with a sensitive and affectionate side. It can show an independent sporting streak, then settle into a dignified gentleness with its people; its unusual name came from a terrier-keeping character in Sir Walter Scott’s novel Guy Mannering.
VBO:0200429.shortDescription: Determined and persistent at work, the Dandie Dinmont Terrier also shows sensitivity and affection with its people.

VBO:0200431.summary: Danish Chicken Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200433.summary: Danish Spitz dogs tend to be affectionate and sociable with familiar people, but they may be reserved and vocal when someone new approaches. Long valued around Jutland farms as companions and watchdogs, they generally stay close to home and have a relatively modest hunting urge.
VBO:0200433.shortDescription: Affectionate with family and watchful of newcomers, this Danish farm companion tends to stay near home.
VBO:0200433.historicalRoots: Danish and Jutland farm companion and watchdog heritage.

VBO:0200434.summary: Danish White Spitz is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200436.summary: Denmark Feist is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200437.summary: Calm and good-natured, Deutsch Langhaars work across field, forest and water, before and after a shot. Their ancestry combines dogs used for birds, falconry and water work with German scent hounds. Breeders began keeping the line pure in 1879, and Baron von Schorlemer wrote its first standard in 1897.
VBO:0200437.shortDescription: Calm and good-natured, this long-haired German pointer works field, forest and water.
VBO:0200437.historicalRoots: German versatile long-haired pointing dog, with documented pure breeding from 1879.

VBO:0200440.summary: Deutscher Wachtelhunds are lively, friendly and assured, selected to flush game from cover and track wounded quarry. The breed works independently while keeping contact with a handler, using voice and nose in woods and water. Its German stud-book history began around the turn of the twentieth century, with brown and roan strains maintained as distinct color lines.
VBO:0200440.shortDescription: Lively and assured, this German flushing dog uses nose and voice in woodland cover and water.
VBO:0200440.historicalRoots: German flushing and tracking dog with stud-book breeding from around 1900.

VBO:0200441.summary: Dingo is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200442.summary: The Doberman tends to be calm and devoted in familiar company while staying attentive to its surroundings. Friedrich Louis Dobermann developed his namesake dog in nineteenth-century Germany for protective work, and the breed later served police forces. Confidence, willingness to work and responsiveness to training helped carry it into demanding service roles.
VBO:0200442.shortDescription: Calm and devoted with familiar people, the Doberman stays attentive and responsive, traits valued in protective and police work.
VBO:0200442.interestingFact: Early police service gave the Doberman the nickname “Gendarme dog.”
VBO:0200442.historicalRoots: German protective working dog developed by Friedrich Louis Dobermann.

VBO:0200443.summary: Calm and devoted to familiar people, the black-and-rust Dobermann is alert, confident and keen to work. Friedrich Louis Dobermann developed the breed in 1870s Germany from protective working dogs. It went on to serve as a guard and police dog, earning the nickname 'Gendarme dog.'
VBO:0200443.shortDescription: Calm and devoted, this black-and-rust Dobermann carries an alert working character and police history.
VBO:0200443.historicalRoots: German working breed developed by Friedrich Louis Dobermann in the 1870s; later used as a guard and police dog.

VBO:0200444.summary: Friendly and steady with familiar people, the brown-and-rust Dobermann shares the breed's self-confident, attentive working character. Friedrich Louis Dobermann built this German line from protective working dogs in the 1870s. Later guard and police work made the breed known as the 'Gendarme dog.'
VBO:0200444.shortDescription: Friendly, steady and attentive, this brown-and-rust Dobermann shares the breed's German working roots.
VBO:0200444.historicalRoots: German breed shaped in the 1870s for protective work and later police service; brown with rust-red markings is an FCI-recognized variety.

VBO:0200445.summary: Courageous and steady under pressure, the Dogo Argentino was bred for big-game hunting in Córdoba. It follows scent across difficult ground and tends to stay quiet on the trail; its breeding tradition also prizes restraint toward people, distinguishing hunting nerve from indiscriminate hostility.
VBO:0200445.shortDescription: Courageous and steady under pressure, the Dogo Argentino follows big game by scent, often staying quiet on the trail.
VBO:0200445.historicalRoots: Córdoba big-game hunting dog developed in the twentieth century.

VBO:0200446.summary: Dogo Cubano is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200447.summary: Calm and loyal with familiar people, the Dogo Guatemalteco may scrutinize strangers before relaxing when they are welcomed. It developed in Guatemala for protection, service, and companionship from a mix that included large Bull Terriers, Boxers, and Dalmatians. Family loyalty and alert guarding remain central to its character.
VBO:0200447.shortDescription: Calm and loyal with familiar people, the Dogo Guatemalteco watches strangers closely before relaxing when they are welcomed.
VBO:0200447.interestingFact: For much of the twentieth century the breed was known as the Guatemalan Bull Terrier.
VBO:0200447.historicalRoots: Guatemalan protection and service dog developed in the early twentieth century.

VBO:0200448.summary: Dogo Sardesco is a dog breed or regional type associated with Italy.

VBO:0200449.summary: Dogue Brasileiro is a dog breed or regional type associated with Brazil.

VBO:0200450.summary: The Dogue de Bordeaux tends to be watchful and courageous, often calm and deeply attached to familiar people. It has a long Aquitaine history that includes guarding homes and cattle and, earlier, hunting large game. It nearly disappeared after the world wars before a postwar revival.
VBO:0200450.shortDescription: Watchful and courageous yet calm with its people, the Dogue de Bordeaux has a long Aquitaine history of guarding and hunting.
VBO:0200450.historicalRoots: French molosser of Aquitaine, historically a guard and big-game dog.

VBO:0200452.summary: Dorset Olde Tyme Bulldogge is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200453.summary: The Drentsche Patrijshond is an attentive partner that tends to keep track of its hunter instead of ranging far away. It searches for birds, points and retrieves; as scent strengthens, its tail may make small circles before the dog freezes into a point, a revealing moment in its cooperative field style.
VBO:0200453.shortDescription: Attentive to its hunter, the Drentsche Patrijshond searches for birds, points and retrieves without ranging far away.

VBO:0200454.summary: Keen but even-tempered, the Drever brings steady persistence to a scent trail rather than a burst of speed. It follows deer at a pace that lets hunters keep up on foot and continues working over long tracks and difficult ground. Sweden developed the breed from Westphalian Dachsbrackes for this practical hunting style.
VBO:0200454.shortDescription: Keen and even-tempered, the Drever follows deer scent steadily, at a pace that lets hunters keep up on foot.
VBO:0200454.historicalRoots: Swedish deer-tracking hound from Westphalian Dachsbracke stock.

VBO:0200455.summary: Dumfriesshire Black and Tan Foxhound is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200456.summary: The Dunker tends to be sociable and trusting as well as robust on a hunt, with a steady manner that has served in field trials. Wilhelm Conrad Dunker developed his Norwegian scent hound for hare hunting, bringing together local working lines in the nineteenth century. Later controlled outcrossing helped maintain genetic variety in a small population.
VBO:0200456.shortDescription: Sociable and trusting, the Dunker is a robust Norwegian hare hound with a steady manner in the field.
VBO:0200456.historicalRoots: Norwegian hare hound developed by Wilhelm Conrad Dunker.

VBO:0200457.summary: Dutch Dachsbracke is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200463.summary: Alert, independent and persistent, the Dutch Shepherd could work with a shepherd yet make decisions without one. It once served as a living fence along crop edges, keeping sheep off the fields, and also moved flocks to market; that mix of initiative and cooperation remains central to its character.
VBO:0200463.shortDescription: Alert and independent, the Dutch Shepherd once kept sheep away from crops like a living fence while working with its shepherd.
VBO:0200463.historicalRoots: Dutch sheep and farm-boundary working dog.

VBO:0200464.summary: Watchful and independent, Dutch Shepherds also have a strong tradition of working closely with people. Their first work included keeping sheep away from crops by patrolling field and road edges, then moving flocks to common grazing. The long-haired variety shares that character and history with the other coat varieties.
VBO:0200464.shortDescription: A watchful sheepdog once tasked with patrolling field edges to keep flocks out of crops, here in its long-haired coat.

VBO:0200465.summary: Rough-haired Dutch Shepherds share the breed’s loyal, alert nature and its habit of working independently while cooperating with a handler. On Dutch farms they patrolled the edges of crops to hold sheep back and kept hens out of kitchen gardens. As flocks declined, Dutch Shepherds also took on police, search and guide work.
VBO:0200465.shortDescription: Loyal and alert, this rough-coated Dutch worker once guarded crop edges, tended flocks and worked with its handler.
VBO:0200465.historicalRoots: Dutch farm shepherd; later police, tracking and guide work as sheep flocks declined.

VBO:0200466.summary: Short-haired Dutch Shepherds share the breed’s watchful, active character and its independent but cooperative working style. On Dutch farms they patrolled field edges to keep sheep from crops and gathered cows for milking. As flocks dwindled, Dutch Shepherds took on police, tracking and guide work; short hair identifies a coat variety.
VBO:0200466.shortDescription: Watchful and cooperative, this short-coated Dutch farm worker guided livestock and patrolled crop edges.
VBO:0200466.historicalRoots: Dutch farm shepherd later used in search, police and guide roles; short coat variety.

VBO:0200467.summary: Dutch Smoushond is a dog breed or regional type associated with Netherlands.

VBO:0200469.summary: Dutch Tulip Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with Netherlands.

VBO:0200471.summary: East Russian Coursing Hounds is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200472.summary: East Siberian Laikas tend to be steady with people while remaining vigorous and independent on a hunt. Their keen scent and strong interest in game developed in the taiga and mountain regions of Central and East Siberia, where the breed has long served as an all-round hunting partner.
VBO:0200472.shortDescription: A steady companion to people, this Siberian laika becomes a vigorous, independent hunter in taiga and mountain country.

VBO:0200473.summary: East-European Shepherd Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200474.summary: Eastern Greyhound is a dog breed or regional type associated with Ukraine.

VBO:0200475.summary: Ecuadorian Hairless Dog is a dog breed or regional type associated with Ecuador.

VBO:0200476.summary: Egyptian Sheepdog is a dog breed or regional type associated with Egypt.

VBO:0200477.summary: Elizabethan Beagle is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200478.summary: Elkhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200479.summary: Elo is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200481.summary: English Boxer is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200482.summary: English Bull Terrier, Coloured is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200483.summary: English Bull Terrier, White is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200484.summary: English Bullador is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200486.summary: Gentle and affectionate with familiar people, English Cocker Spaniels can become bustling, enthusiastic workers on a scent. They took their name from woodcock, the birds they once flushed from thick cover. Working and show lines differ today, but the impulse to investigate a trail still links them.
VBO:0200486.shortDescription: Gentle and affectionate with familiar people, the English Cocker Spaniel becomes enthusiastic when flushing birds from thick cover.

VBO:0200487.summary: English Cocker Spaniel, Particolours (Bicolours, Tricolours, Roans) is a variety of English Cocker Spaniel.

VBO:0200488.summary: English Cocker Spaniels are gentle and affectionate, yet exuberant when a scent catches them. Their bustling movement and fearless way through heavy cover come from work flushing woodcock; the breed’s name comes from that bird. The standard describes an ever-wagging tail, especially as they follow scent.
VBO:0200488.shortDescription: Gentle and affectionate, this merry spaniel was bred to flush woodcock from dense cover.

VBO:0200490.summary: The English Foxhound tends to be friendly and sociable, with the stamina and natural hunting drive to keep pace in a pack. It was developed for long collective work on fox scent during mounted hunts. English hunt masters kept pedigrees for generations, leaving studbooks that reach back before 1800.
VBO:0200490.shortDescription: Friendly and sociable, the English Foxhound works with a pack, following fox scent over long mounted hunts.
VBO:0200490.historicalRoots: English pack hound with documented fox-hunting lines.

VBO:0200493.summary: English Mastweiler is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200495.summary: The English Setter is often intensely friendly with people while remaining active and keen for game. In the field it searches for birds and holds a point so the hunter can approach; its open social manner and focused working drive are both longstanding parts of the breed's identity.
VBO:0200495.shortDescription: Friendly with people yet keen for game, the English Setter searches for birds and holds a point until the hunter approaches.

VBO:0200496.summary: English Shepherds often meet farm work with calm independence while staying closely tuned to their handler. They can gather or drive stock in an upright, loose-eyed style, choosing the pressure the task needs rather than fixing on one approach. Generations of all-purpose farm work also called on them to guard the home and deal with vermin.
VBO:0200496.shortDescription: Calm and independent on the farm, the English Shepherd handles stock with a loose eye and stays attuned to its handler.

VBO:0200497.summary: Eager and cooperative, English Springer Spaniels tend to work closely with a handler when finding and flushing game. Before guns changed the hunt, their ancestors sprang birds for nets, falcons, or greyhounds; the breed later became a flushing and retrieving gun dog. Its active nature is rooted in that long partnership in the field.
VBO:0200497.shortDescription: Eager and cooperative, the English Springer Spaniel works close to a handler to find and flush game, then retrieve it.

VBO:0200499.summary: Alert and distinctly terrier-like, the English Toy Terrier tends to meet the world with quick attention without being unduly nervous. That alertness has a working history: earlier dogs performed in rat pits, a demanding task behind this small breed’s confident presence.
VBO:0200499.shortDescription: Alert without undue nervousness, the English Toy Terrier retains quick terrier attention from its ratting history.
VBO:0200499.historicalRoots: British toy terrier with historic rat-pit work

VBO:0200500.summary: English Water Spaniel is a dog breed or regional type associated with United Kingdom.

VBO:0200501.summary: English White Terrier is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200502.summary: The Entlebuch Cattle Dog tends to be lively and confident, devoted to familiar faces yet somewhat suspicious of strangers. It comes from a Swiss valley where it drove stock, watched farms and worked close to people. Both driving cattle and watching the farm rewarded a dog that noticed changes quickly and stayed close to its people.
VBO:0200502.shortDescription: Lively and confident with familiar people, the Entlebuch Cattle Dog drove Swiss stock and watched farms, staying alert to changes.
VBO:0200502.historicalRoots: Swiss Entlebuch valley stock driver and farm guard.

VBO:0200506.summary: Epagneul Pont-Audemer is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200508.summary: The Estonian Hound is generally friendly and even-tempered, with agility that serves it well when following a scent. It was shaped for difficult forest country, where a resonant voice helps hunters locate a dog out of sight; its development also sought a smaller local hound suited to Estonian conditions.
VBO:0200508.shortDescription: Friendly and even-tempered, the Estonian Hound follows scent through difficult forest country, using its voice to guide hunters.
VBO:0200508.historicalRoots: Estonian hare, fox and lynx hound standardized in 1954.

VBO:0200509.summary: Close to their own shepherd and cautious with strangers, Estrela Mountain Dogs bring an attentive judgment to flock protection. They traveled with Portuguese flocks between valley and high pasture, guarding against predators and thieves.
VBO:0200509.shortDescription: Close to its shepherd but cautious with strangers, the Estrela Mountain Dog guarded Portuguese flocks between valleys and high pasture.
VBO:0200509.interestingFact: Traditional summer pasture in the Estrela Mountains can reach roughly 2,000 meters.

VBO:0200510.summary: Estrela Mountain Dog, Long-Haired is a variety of Estrela Mountain Dog.

VBO:0200511.summary: Estrela Mountain Dog, Short-Haired is a variety of Estrela Mountain Dog.

VBO:0200512.summary: The Eurasier tends to be calm and closely attached to family, attentive without constant noise and more reserved than pushy with strangers. German breeders developed it specifically for companionship, beginning with Chow Chow and Wolfspitz crosses and later adding Samoyed. Quiet watchfulness remains part of that companion role.
VBO:0200512.shortDescription: Calm and closely attached to family, the Eurasier watches quietly and tends to be reserved rather than pushy with strangers.
VBO:0200512.interestingFact: It was first called the Wolf-Chow before the Samoyed cross led to the Eurasier name.
VBO:0200512.historicalRoots: German companion spitz founded by Julius Wipfel in the 1960s.

VBO:0200515.summary: Feist is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200516.summary: Fell Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200517.summary: Fell Terrier, Black is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200518.summary: Fell Terrier, Red is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200519.summary: Field Spaniels are often notably docile and sensitive, yet capable of independent decisions while working. A rough-shooting hunter relies on one to search cover, flush game and retrieve it; the breed's practical character survived two severe declines through deliberate efforts to rebuild it.
VBO:0200519.shortDescription: Docile and sensitive yet capable of independent decisions, the Field Spaniel searches cover, flushes game and retrieves it.

VBO:0200520.summary: Calm and self-assured with familiar people, the Fila Brasileiro is also markedly vigilant in unfamiliar situations. Its Brazilian history combines watching, protection, and the courage to face large game. Steady nerves and alert judgment mattered as much as force in those demanding working roles.
VBO:0200520.shortDescription: Calm and self-assured with familiar people, the Fila Brasileiro remains vigilant in unfamiliar situations, reflecting its guarding work.

VBO:0200521.summary: Fila da Terceira is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200522.summary: Finnish Hounds are calm, friendly dogs with an energetic, independent style on a scent trail. Developed in Finland during the nineteenth century, they traditionally hunt hare and fox and give voice while following a trail; the breed standard records the first written standard in 1932.
VBO:0200522.shortDescription: Friendly and independent on a scent, the Finnish Hound traditionally trails hare and fox with a ringing voice.

VBO:0200523.summary: The Finnish Lapphund tends to combine courage and calm with a friendly, responsive manner, a useful balance around shifting livestock and people. It grew from dogs Sámi communities used to herd reindeer across northern Fennoscandia. In Finland it has also become a familiar companion, while that northern working history remains central.
VBO:0200523.shortDescription: Courageous and calm with a friendly manner, the Finnish Lapphund grew from Sámi dogs used to herd reindeer.
VBO:0200523.historicalRoots: Sámi reindeer-herding tradition in northern Fennoscandia.

VBO:0200525.summary: Finnish Reindeer Herder is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200526.summary: Finnish Spitz are lively, determined hunters with an independent streak; they can be reserved when meeting strangers. Their distinctive skill is locating game birds in trees and marking the spot by barking, working at a distance while keeping the hunter informed. That purposeful use of their voice is woven into the breed’s character and working tradition.
VBO:0200526.shortDescription: Lively and independent, the Finnish Spitz locates birds in trees and barks to mark their position for a hunter.
VBO:0200526.interestingFact: Finland named the Finnish Spitz its national dog in 1979.
VBO:0200526.historicalRoots: Finnish spitz-type hunting dog used to indicate game birds in trees.

VBO:0200528.summary: Optimism is a memorable Flat-Coated Retriever trait: the breed is usually friendly, confident and ready for another job. It was shaped for retrieving shot game, including birds and hare, so its buoyant manner sits alongside the stamina and purpose needed for a long day afield.
VBO:0200528.shortDescription: Friendly, confident and ready for work, the Flat-Coated Retriever brings optimism and stamina to retrieving game.

VBO:0200529.summary: Keenly alert and quick to react, the Formosan Mountain Dog retains the attention valued in Taiwan’s central mountain hunting dogs. Its roots trace to dogs that accompanied hunters through forest terrain, where noticing movement and keeping up with people mattered. The breed’s native identity was documented again in a 1980 university survey.
VBO:0200529.shortDescription: Keenly alert and quick to react, the Formosan Mountain Dog reflects Taiwan's forest hunting tradition.

VBO:0200530.summary: Fox Terrier is a dog breed or regional type associated with United Kingdom.

VBO:0200531.summary: Foxhound is a dog breed or regional type associated with England.

VBO:0200533.summary: French Basset is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200534.summary: French Brittany is a variety of Brittany associated with Brittany.

VBO:0200536.summary: French Bull Terrier is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0200537.summary: Gascon Saintongeois hounds are calm, affectionate pack workers with a fine nose and a distinctive carrying voice. The Grand line arose in nineteenth-century southwestern France when the last Saintonge hounds were crossed with Bleu de Gascogne; the Petit was later selected from smaller Grand hounds.
VBO:0200537.shortDescription: Calm and fine-nosed, this southwestern French pack hound is known for a far-carrying voice on the trail.

VBO:0200538.summary: French Bulldog, Fawn, Brindled Or Not, With Medium Or Predominant Patching is a variety of French Bulldog.

VBO:0200544.summary: French Pointer is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200547.summary: French Sheepdog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200548.summary: French Spaniels are calm and gentle in company but enthusiastic in the field, where their firm point and retrieving ability come to the fore. Their ancestors appear in medieval French hunting accounts; later selection shaped the athletic pointing dog described today.
VBO:0200548.shortDescription: Gentle in company and keen in the field, the French Spaniel has a long tradition of pointing and retrieving.

VBO:0200549.summary: French Tricolour Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0200550.summary: The French Water Dog, or Barbet, is often sociable and closely attached to its handler, with a particular eagerness for water. It searches marshy vegetation, flushes birds and retrieves them even in cold conditions; that affinity for wet work is a living part of its temperament and history.
VBO:0200550.shortDescription: Sociable and close to its handler, the French Water Dog eagerly searches marshes, flushes birds and retrieves in cold water.
VBO:0200550.historicalRoots: French waterfowl flushing and retrieving dog.

VBO:0200551.summary: French White and Black Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0200552.summary: French White and Orange Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0200556.summary: Fuegian Dog is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0200557.summary: Serious or reserved away from the chase, the Galgo Español becomes lively and energetic in hunting work. This Spanish sighthound was shaped by open-field hare pursuit, where keen sight and sustained effort mattered. The contrast between quiet company and determined coursing is a memorable part of its character.
VBO:0200557.shortDescription: Reserved away from a chase, the Galgo Español becomes lively in open-field hare pursuit, relying on sight and sustained effort.

VBO:0200558.summary: Garafian Shepherd is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200559.summary: Gascogne Braque Français is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0200561.summary: Gascon Saintongeois, Great is a variety of Gascon Saintongeois associated with France.

VBO:0200562.summary: Gascon Saintongeois, Small is a variety of Gascon Saintongeois associated with France.

VBO:0200563.summary: The Georgian Shepherd tends to be watchful and capable of independent action, enduring harsh conditions as it guards. Also called the Kartuli Nagazi, it developed in Georgia’s mountains as a protective dog for people and holdings. Its work called for noticing danger, making decisions and staying on duty across scattered mountain communities.
VBO:0200563.shortDescription: Watchful and independently minded, the Georgian Shepherd guarded people and holdings across demanding mountain country.
VBO:0200563.historicalRoots: Georgian mountain guardian and pastoral dog.

VBO:0200567.summary: German Hounds follow scent with a clear voice, an old Bracke trait prized during their long hare-hunting history. Around 1900, breeders joined the Sauerländer Holzbracke with local Steinbracken to establish the Deutsche Bracke. The breed now also works driven hunts, where its reliable trail voice remains valued.
VBO:0200567.shortDescription: Vocal on a scent trail, the tricolor Deutsche Bracke carries an old German hare-hunting tradition.
VBO:0200567.historicalRoots: German Deutsche Bracke formed by Westphalian and local Steinbracke lines around 1900.

VBO:0200569.summary: German Koolie is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200570.summary: German Longhaired Pointer is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200572.summary: German Pinschers are lively, self-assured and even-tempered, with the alertness to serve as watchdogs while remaining close family companions. The smooth-coated pinscher appeared in German stud records by 1880 and shares its ancestry with the rough-coated line that became the Schnauzer; black and tan is one of its recognized colors.
VBO:0200572.shortDescription: Lively and self-assured, this black-and-tan Pinscher brings watchfulness to family life.
VBO:0200572.historicalRoots: German smooth-coated pinscher recorded by 1880; black-and-tan color variety.

VBO:0200573.summary: German Pinschers are spirited and intelligent without losing the even temper of a companion. Their endurance and quick attention also suit the breed's traditional watchdog role. This self-colored red variety belongs to the same smooth-coated German line recorded in the stud book by 1880, alongside the black-and-tan dogs.
VBO:0200573.shortDescription: Spirited, intelligent and even-tempered, this red Pinscher has a German watchdog heritage.
VBO:0200573.historicalRoots: German smooth-coated pinscher recorded by 1880; self-colored red variety.

VBO:0200574.summary: German Pointer is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200575.summary: German Roughhaired Pointers are calm, self-controlled and courageous gundogs that remain tractable while working. Also called Deutsch Stichelhaar, the breed descends from an old rough-coated German partridge-dog line rather than the German Shorthaired Pointer. In 1888, Hans von Kadisch established that separate lineage; breeders later rebuilt the type from a small surviving population.
VBO:0200575.shortDescription: Calm and self-controlled, the Deutsch Stichelhaar follows an old German pointing line distinct from the shorthaired pointer.

VBO:0200576.summary: German Sheeppoodle is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0200577.summary: Steadily attentive and willing to work beside a handler, the German Shepherd Dog grew from versatile German herding stock. Its role expanded into protection and other service work, asking for focus in changing situations. That ability to shift tasks while remaining responsive to human direction is central to its working identity.
VBO:0200577.shortDescription: Steadily attentive and responsive to a handler, the German Shepherd Dog moved from herding into protection and service work.

VBO:0200578.summary: Self-assured and attentive, double-coated German Shepherds combine a watchful manner with a willingness to follow direction. Developed from central and southern German herding dogs, the breed’s organized breeding began in 1899 with a clear aim: a capable working dog whose character mattered as much as its build.
VBO:0200578.shortDescription: Attentive and self-assured, this German herding dog was developed for working character as well as sound structure.
VBO:0200578.historicalRoots: Developed in Germany from regional herding dogs after the founding of the breed club in 1899; double coat is one FCI-recognized coat variety.

VBO:0200579.summary: Attentive and self-assured, long-coated German Shepherds share the breed’s responsive, even-tempered character. Their roots lie in central and southern German herding dogs, brought together in a deliberate breeding program for demanding work; the longer coat is one of two recognized varieties.
VBO:0200579.shortDescription: Self-assured and responsive, the long-coated German Shepherd shares a history shaped by demanding herding work.
VBO:0200579.historicalRoots: Developed from regional German herding dogs after 1899; long and harsh outer coat is a recognized variety of the same breed.

VBO:0200580.summary: German Shepherd Dog, Non-White is a variety of German Shepherd Dog.

VBO:0200581.summary: German Shepherd Dog, Old is a variety of German Shepherd Dog.

VBO:0200582.summary: German Shepherd Dog, White is a variety of German Shepherd Dog.

VBO:0200583.summary: The German Shorthaired Pointer tends to be firm, balanced and reliable, with a working temperament that is neither nervous nor easily unsettled. Bred as an all-purpose gundog, it can point game, follow a trail and retrieve after the shot. German breeders used field trials to keep that versatile working ability central.
VBO:0200583.shortDescription: Firm and balanced in temperament, the German Shorthaired Pointer points game, follows trails and retrieves after the shot.
VBO:0200583.historicalRoots: German all-purpose pointing dog refined from European bird-hunting lines.

VBO:0200601.summary: German Spitz, Toy is a variety of German Spitz.

VBO:0200602.summary: Steady nerves and self-control around gunfire are prized in the German Wirehaired Pointer. It moves between searching, pointing and retrieving in field, forest and water, both before and after a shot; the versatile work asks for focus that holds when the surroundings change.
VBO:0200602.shortDescription: Steady around gunfire, the German Wirehaired Pointer stays focused while searching, pointing and retrieving across field, forest and water.
VBO:0200602.historicalRoots: German all-terrain pointing and retrieving gundog.

VBO:0200603.summary: German Wolfspitz is a variety of German Spitz.

VBO:0200604.summary: Energetic yet composed, the Giant Schnauzer tends to bring loyalty and endurance to demanding work. It first drove cattle in southern Germany and later took on broader utility roles. Its capacity to stay focused through a long task grew alongside a close working partnership with people.
VBO:0200604.shortDescription: Energetic yet composed, the Giant Schnauzer brings loyalty and endurance from its cattle-driving roots to demanding work.
VBO:0200604.historicalRoots: Southern German cattle driving and later utility work.

VBO:0200605.summary: Giant Schnauzer, Black And Silver is a variety of Giant Schnauzer.

VBO:0200606.summary: Giant Schnauzers tend to be even-tempered, loyal and self-assured, with keen senses and an eagerness for work. In southern Germany they originally drove cattle, and the breed was formally recognized as a working dog in 1925. Their endurance and trainability remain part of the character described for the breed.
VBO:0200606.shortDescription: Even-tempered and self-assured, this loyal German worker began as a southern cattle driver.

VBO:0200607.summary: Giant Schnauzer, Pure Black With Black Undercoat is a variety of Giant Schnauzer.

VBO:0200608.summary: Giant Schnoodle is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0200609.summary: The Glen of Imaal Terrier often combines courage when needed with a relatively quiet, less easily excited manner than some terriers. It comes from an Irish valley where dogs had to hunt foxes and badgers and help control rats. Older accounts even describe Glen dogs turning wheels in farm households.
VBO:0200609.shortDescription: Courageous but relatively quiet for a terrier, the Glen of Imaal Terrier hunted foxes and badgers in its Irish valley.
VBO:0200609.historicalRoots: Irish Glen of Imaal farm terrier selected for hard local work.

VBO:0200610.summary: Golden Retrievers tend to be friendly, confident and eager to cooperate, with a strong interest in working alongside people. Their retrieving background calls for finding game and bringing it back over land or water. The breed’s Scottish beginnings are unusually well documented in the Guisachan estate records, where practical working ability and a pleasant character helped shape the dogs.
VBO:0200610.shortDescription: Friendly and eager to cooperate, the Golden Retriever works beside people to find and bring back game on land or water.
VBO:0200610.interestingFact: An 1868 mating between Nous and the Tweed Water Spaniel Belle produced the four puppies at the center of the Golden Retriever’s recorded beginnings.
VBO:0200610.historicalRoots: Nineteenth-century Scottish retriever developed for land-and-water gundog work.

VBO:0200611.summary: Goldendoodle is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200613.summary: A Gordon Setter is often bold, outgoing and kindly, as well as alert to game. It searches for birds and holds a point for a hunter; the breed's association with the Duke of Gordon's Scottish kennels gives this active sporting dog a particularly vivid chapter in setter history.
VBO:0200613.shortDescription: Bold, outgoing and kindly, the Gordon Setter searches for birds and holds a point for a hunter.

VBO:0200615.summary: Courageous and independent on a scent trail, the Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen makes its progress known with a ringing voice. It was selected to pursue hare through the brambles and scrub of western France, working with speed as well as persistence in cover. Paul Dezamy helped establish the working type behind this distinctive hound.
VBO:0200615.shortDescription: Courageous and independent on scent, the Grand Basset Griffon Vendéen pursues hare through western French scrub with a ringing voice.
VBO:0200615.historicalRoots: Vendéen hare hound refined from larger griffons.

VBO:0200617.summary: Grand Fauve de Bretagne is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200619.summary: Docile but wilful, the Grand Griffon Vendéen is an assiduous tracker with a fine nose and resonant voice. Built for large hunting territories, it can work through thorny undergrowth while following game; the old Vendéan line carries contributions from several historic French hounds.
VBO:0200619.shortDescription: Docile yet wilful, this large Vendéan hound tracks through thorny cover with a fine nose and carrying voice.
VBO:0200619.historicalRoots: An old French Vendéen scent hound shaped by the Greffier line and other historic French hunting dogs.

VBO:0200620.summary: Great Anglo-French Tricolor Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0200621.summary: Great Anglo-French White and Black Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0200622.summary: Great Anglo-French White and Orange Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0200623.summary: Great Danes tend to be affectionate and closely attached to their people, while sometimes taking a more reserved approach to strangers. Their modern companion role follows a history of boar hunting and guarding. Despite the English name, the breed was developed in Germany, where it is known as the Deutsche Dogge.
VBO:0200623.shortDescription: Affectionate and attached to its people, the Great Dane can be reserved with strangers; its history includes boar hunting and guarding.
VBO:0200623.historicalRoots: German giant dog descended from large hunting and estate types.
