VBO:0200985.summary: Papillon is a variety of Continental Toy Spaniel.

VBO:0200987.summary: Parson Russell Terriers are often confident, energetic and friendly, with the boldness of a dog bred to work below ground. Their fox-working history explains the breed’s agile, persistent style. The name honors the Reverend John Russell, whose Victorian hunting terriers shaped the strain later recognized as a separate breed.
VBO:0200987.shortDescription: Confident and energetic, the Parson Russell Terrier brings fox-working boldness to agile pursuit below ground.
VBO:0200987.historicalRoots: British fox-working terrier associated with Reverend John Russell

VBO:0200988.summary: Pastore della Lessinia e del Lagorai is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200989.summary: Patagonian Sheepdogs were shaped by practical flock work in southern Chile after European sheepdogs reached the region. They still help manage sheep, and sometimes cattle, on widely separated farms; generations of selection and geographic isolation gave this regional working population a history distinct from its imported ancestors.
VBO:0200989.shortDescription: Patagonian Sheepdogs still manage sheep and sometimes cattle on distant Chilean farms, shaped by generations of local work.

VBO:0200990.summary: Patterdale Terriers are bold, active dogs with a strong prey drive and a marked willingness to work with their people. Developed among northern England's fell terriers, they followed quarry into tight burrows and held it at bay; their work was tied to controlling vermin around sheep country.
VBO:0200990.shortDescription: Bold and keen to work, this northern English earth terrier follows quarry into tight burrows.
VBO:0200990.historicalRoots: Northern English Fell Terrier developed for underground vermin work in sheep country.

VBO:0200994.summary: Fearless and loyal to familiar people, the Pekingese has a distinctly self-possessed manner. It was bred for companionship in China and tends to meet strangers with dignified reserve. That combination of closeness and independence gives the small dog a character that can feel larger than its size.
VBO:0200994.shortDescription: Fearless and loyal with familiar people, the Pekingese combines close companionship with dignified reserve toward strangers.

VBO:0200995.summary: The Pembroke Welsh Corgi tends to be bold, outgoing and friendly, with stamina to keep moving as livestock changes direction. It was bred to work sheep and cattle, staying mobile and alert around animals much larger than itself. The farm role rewarded initiative as well as a close response to its handler.
VBO:0200995.shortDescription: Bold and outgoing, the Pembroke Welsh Corgi keeps moving around larger livestock while watching its handler.
VBO:0200995.historicalRoots: Welsh cattle herder with a compact low build.

VBO:0200996.summary: Pencil-Tail Feist is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0200997.summary: Perdiguero de Burgos dogs are calm, docile hunters with a strong nose and a firm, persistent way of following a trail. The Spanish pointer is valued for pointing and retrieving feathered and small game across difficult ground. Though usually trained for smaller quarry, the breed also has a history of boldly tackling larger game.
VBO:0200997.shortDescription: Calm and persistent, this Burgos pointer uses a keen nose to track, point and retrieve across rough ground.

VBO:0201003.summary: Perro Majoreros tend to be loyal and strongly territorial, warm with familiar people but wary of strangers. On Fuerteventura they directed livestock without harming it and guarded property; their sure-footed movement over rough lava ground was part of that working life.
VBO:0201003.shortDescription: Loyal to familiar people and wary of strangers, this Fuerteventura worker herded stock and watched property.
VBO:0201003.historicalRoots: Fuerteventura livestock driving and property guarding on rough volcanic terrain.

VBO:0201004.summary: Peruvian Hairless Dogs tend to be affectionate with their own people and more cautious around strangers, combining close companionship with an alert watchdog instinct. Their cultural history reaches far beyond the modern breed: depictions appear in the ceramics of several pre-Inca societies, including the Moche and Chancay.
VBO:0201004.shortDescription: Affectionate with familiar people but cautious with strangers, this Peruvian dog combines companionship with alert watchfulness.
VBO:0201004.interestingFact: Viringo is another name for the Peruvian Hairless Dog.
VBO:0201004.historicalRoots: Ancient Peruvian hairless-dog tradition documented in pre-Columbian art.

VBO:0201005.summary: Peruvian Hairless Dog, Large is a variety of Peruvian Hairless Dog.

VBO:0201006.summary: Peruvian Hairless Dog, Medium-Sized is a variety of Peruvian Hairless Dog.

VBO:0201007.summary: Peruvian Hairless Dog, Miniature is a variety of Peruvian Hairless Dog.

VBO:0201009.summary: Petit Basset Griffon Vendeen is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0201010.summary: Petit Bleu de Gascogne is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0201011.summary: Petit Brabançon is a variety of Brussels Griffon.

VBO:0201013.summary: Petit Griffon Bleu de Gascogne is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201014.summary: Petite Goldendoodle is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0201015.summary: Phalène is a variety of Continental Toy Spaniel associated with Belgium.

VBO:0201016.summary: Alert and playful away from a hunt, the Pharaoh Hound is often affectionate with familiar people. In Malta it pursues small game by sight, scent and hearing, using its ears to locate quarry among rocky fields; the living island hunting practice gives the breed a story beyond its ancient-looking name.
VBO:0201016.shortDescription: Playful with familiar people, the Pharaoh Hound hunts small Maltese game by sight, scent, and hearing among rocky fields.

VBO:0201017.summary: Phu Quoc Ridgeback is a dog breed or regional type associated with Vietnam.

VBO:0201019.summary: Picardy Spaniels tend to be gentle and even-tempered, with the energy of an athletic pointing dog. Hunters in Picardy valued a keen nose and a steady point for small game across the region’s fields and marshes. The breed remained largely local for generations, then drew renewed interest from hunters who appreciated that versatile field work.
VBO:0201019.shortDescription: Gentle yet energetic, the Picardy Spaniel used its keen nose and steady point across northern French fields and marshes.
VBO:0201019.historicalRoots: Regional French pointing spaniel used for small game across Picardy's varied terrain.

VBO:0201020.summary: Pila is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201021.summary: Pinscher is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201023.summary: Loyal, alert and eager to please, Plott Hounds also have a bold, fearless hunting tradition. The Plott family developed these scent hounds in the North Carolina mountains, where they tracked bears and mountain lions; their ancestors had hunted wild boar in Germany.
VBO:0201023.shortDescription: Loyal and alert with a bold hunting streak, this scent hound carries a North Carolina mountain legacy.
VBO:0201023.historicalRoots: Developed by the Plott family in North Carolina’s Appalachian region for big-game hunting.

VBO:0201024.summary: Plummer Terriers tend to be active, alert and tenacious, yet affectionate with family and familiar people. Brian Plummer developed the breed in the 1960s for practical terrier work; its breed club still emphasizes searching for and controlling vermin both above and below ground.
VBO:0201024.shortDescription: Active and tenacious in terrier work, the Plummer is also affectionate with familiar people.
VBO:0201024.historicalRoots: Modern British working terrier developed by Brian Plummer from the 1960s.

VBO:0201025.summary: Pocket Beagle is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201026.summary: Podenco is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201027.summary: Podencos Canarios are energetic, courageous rabbit hunters, using nose, sight and hearing together across broken volcanic terrain. Strongly attached to their handler, they can locate rabbits hidden in rock crevices and lava tubes.
VBO:0201027.shortDescription: This energetic Canarian rabbit hunter combines nose, sight and hearing to search crevices and volcanic terrain.

VBO:0201028.summary: Podenco Valenciano is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201029.summary: Keenly aware of game and gentle in ordinary company, the Pointer combines field intensity with an even manner. It finds quarry and holds a still, directed point that tells a hunter exactly where to look. Endurance over long stretches of British hunting ground made that precise signal useful far beyond a brief burst of speed.
VBO:0201029.shortDescription: Gentle in company but intent in the field, the Pointer holds a still, directed signal when it finds game.

VBO:0201030.summary: Pointer-Rottweiler Mix is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0201031.summary: Poitevin is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0201032.summary: The Chart Polski tends to be self-assured, brave and sometimes reserved rather than immediately familiar. In pursuit it is fast, skillful and tireless, reacting quickly when game moves. This Polish hunting sighthound appears in records from the thirteenth century, giving its chase instinct a long regional history.
VBO:0201032.shortDescription: Self-assured and sometimes reserved, the Polish Greyhound brings swift reactions and tireless pursuit to the chase.
VBO:0201032.historicalRoots: Polish hunting sighthound documented since the medieval period.

VBO:0201033.summary: Polish Hounds are devoted to their household yet often wary of strangers. On a fresh trail they give tongue loudly as they pursue game, a voice Polish hunters have long treated as part of the chase. This heavier Ogar line once served royal hunts; today its work in Poland centers on wild boar and fox rather than the hares it historically followed.
VBO:0201033.shortDescription: Devoted at home and vocal on a fresh trail, the heavier Polish Ogar once served royal hunts.
VBO:0201033.historicalRoots: Old-established Polish Ogar hound, historically linked to royal hunting and now used for boar and fox.

VBO:0201034.summary: Polish Hunting Dogs tend to be steady and gentle, yet courageous on a hunt and watchful around strangers. Their voice changes pitch while following game, a working signal in the forests and difficult southern Polish mountains where they pursued boar and deer. This lithe Gończy type developed separately from the heavier Polish Ogar hound.
VBO:0201034.shortDescription: Steady and gentle, the leaner Polish Gończy gives a changing voice while pursuing game in mountain forests.
VBO:0201034.historicalRoots: Lighter Gończy Polski scent hound retained for boar and deer work in difficult southern Polish mountain terrain.

VBO:0201035.summary: The Polish Lowland Sheepdog is often lively, vigilant and quick to remember what matters around a flock. It both moves sheep and watches over them, using close attention to the shepherd and surroundings; that perceptive character also fits the breed's traditional farm-guard role.
VBO:0201035.shortDescription: Lively and vigilant, this Polish sheepdog moves flocks while watching both the shepherd and nearby activity.
VBO:0201035.historicalRoots: Polish lowland herding and farm-watch dog.

VBO:0201036.summary: Polish Sheepdog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201037.summary: Polish Tatra Sheepdog is a dog breed or regional type associated with Poland.

VBO:0201038.summary: Polynesian Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201043.summary: Attentive and lively, the Pomeranian tends to learn quickly and raise an alarm when household activity changes. It is the toy-sized German Spitz, sharing a family history with larger spitz dogs while carrying its own close companion role. Its alert interest in people and surroundings remains its defining everyday trait.
VBO:0201043.shortDescription: Lively and quick to learn, the Pomeranian raises an alarm when household activity changes.

VBO:0201044.summary: Pomeranian-Chow Chow Mix is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0201046.summary: Pont-Audemer Spaniels worked close to their hunters, searching and pointing without ranging far ahead. In Normandy’s Vernier marshes they became known for waterfowl work and retrieving, but they also hunted in woods and open country.
VBO:0201046.shortDescription: A close-working Norman spaniel, at home searching marshes for waterfowl and retrieving from the water.
VBO:0201046.historicalRoots: Norman pointing and water dog associated with the Vernier marshes and fowl hunting.

VBO:0201048.summary: The Poodle tends to be loyal and quick to learn, carrying cooperative traits from its waterfowl-hunting roots into work and play. It once entered water to retrieve birds, then became a notably trainable companion. The French name caniche still points back to ducks and the breed’s old retrieving role.
VBO:0201048.shortDescription: Loyal and quick to learn, the Poodle carries cooperation from waterfowl retrieving into work and play.
VBO:0201048.historicalRoots: French waterfowl dog of Barbet-related ancestry, later a companion in four sizes.

VBO:0201049.summary: Poodle, Medium size Brown Black White is a variety of Poodle.

VBO:0201050.summary: Poodle, Medium size Grey Fawn is a variety of Poodle.

VBO:0201051.summary: Loyal and quick to learn, the Miniature Poodle carries the same lively, capable character described for the Poodle breed in a smaller frame. Poodles have a water-retrieving heritage; modern Miniatures can channel that alertness into training, games and other activities beyond their familiar clipped appearance.
VBO:0201051.shortDescription: Loyal and quick to learn, this smaller Poodle shares the breed’s lively character and water-dog heritage.
VBO:0201051.historicalRoots: The Miniature is a size variety of the Poodle, a European water-retrieving breed with a long companion history.

VBO:0201052.summary: Poodle, Miniature Brown Black White is a variety of Poodle, Miniature.

VBO:0201053.summary: Poodle, Miniature Grey Fawn is a variety of Poodle, Miniature.

VBO:0201055.summary: Poodle, Multi-Colored is a variety of Poodle associated with France.

VBO:0201056.summary: Standard Poodles are often joyful and loyal, with a quick capacity to learn that helped them move from water work into life as companions. Their French name, caniche, recalls ducks: the breed was once used for wildfowling before its sizes and styles diversified.
VBO:0201056.shortDescription: Joyful and quick to learn, the Standard Poodle carries a waterfowling heritage into companion life.
VBO:0201056.historicalRoots: Largest Poodle variety; French waterfowling ancestry and later companion role.

VBO:0201057.summary: Poodle, Standard Brown Black White is a variety of Poodle, Standard.

VBO:0201058.summary: Poodle, Standard Grey Fawn is a variety of Poodle, Standard.

VBO:0201059.summary: Poodle, Standard Multi-Colored is a variety of Poodle, Standard.

VBO:0201060.summary: Poodle, Teacup is a variety of Poodle.

VBO:0201061.summary: Loyal, lively and receptive to training, the Toy Poodle shares the Poodle’s keen learning ability despite its tiny size. Smaller Poodles became city companions in Europe, and the Toy variety was bred in the United States in the early twentieth century; its lineage still reaches back to European water dogs.
VBO:0201061.shortDescription: Tiny but lively and quick to learn, the Toy Poodle shares its larger relatives’ loyal character and water-dog roots.
VBO:0201061.historicalRoots: The smallest Poodle size variety, bred in the United States in the early twentieth century from the older European Poodle water-dog line.

VBO:0201064.summary: The Porcelaine follows small-game scent through French hunting country and drives quarry toward hunters waiting ahead. It does a different job from a pointing dog: the chase must continue long enough for people to position themselves, and the hound's skill lies in keeping that moving trail alive.
VBO:0201064.shortDescription: The Porcelaine keeps a small-game scent trail moving through French hunting country, driving quarry toward waiting hunters.

VBO:0201067.summary: Watchful and resourceful, the Portuguese Podengo is a family of hunting dogs rather than one fixed working style. Large Podengos pursued bigger game, medium ones worked rabbits alone or in packs, and small ones searched holes and rocks. Alert companionship links these varied working traditions.
VBO:0201067.shortDescription: Watchful and resourceful, Podengos vary in hunting style, from larger game pursuit to searching rabbit holes and rocks.
VBO:0201067.historicalRoots: Portuguese warren and other hunting traditions.

VBO:0201068.summary: Portuguese Podengo Pequeno is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201069.summary: Portuguese Pointers are affectionate, curious hunters that work persistently while keeping close contact with the hunter. Their pointing role is documented in Portugal by the fourteenth century, when the dog was known as the “podengo de mostra”; falconry and later partridge hunting also shaped its history.
VBO:0201069.shortDescription: An affectionate, curious pointer that hunts persistently while keeping close contact with the person in the field.

VBO:0201070.summary: Portuguese Rabbit Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201071.summary: The Portuguese Sheepdog tends to be lively and deeply focused on its shepherd and herd, with a watchful streak that helped alert to predators. It worked the Alentejo plains, keeping sheep, cattle, goats, horses and pigs together and searching for strays. That range of livestock and the distances between pastures made versatility essential.
VBO:0201071.shortDescription: Lively and focused on shepherd and herd, this Portuguese worker kept varied livestock together across Alentejo pastures.
VBO:0201071.historicalRoots: Alentejo all-purpose livestock herder and watcher.

VBO:0201074.summary: Portuguese Warren Hound-Portuguese Podengo, Large is a variety of Portuguese Podengo.

VBO:0201075.summary: Portuguese Warren Hound-Portuguese Podengo, Medium-Sized is a variety of Portuguese Podengo.

VBO:0201076.summary: Portuguese Warren Hound-Portuguese Podengo, Small is a variety of Portuguese Podengo.

VBO:0201077.summary: Portuguese Water Dogs are often intelligent and vigorous, with an independent streak that can shade into wilfulness. They worked beside fishermen, carrying messages between boats and retrieving gear from the water; a willingness to swim and dive made them especially useful along Portugal's Algarve coast.
VBO:0201077.shortDescription: Vigorous and independent, the Portuguese Water Dog carried messages between fishing boats and retrieved gear from the sea.

VBO:0201078.summary: Portuguese Water Dog, Long And Wavy is a variety of Portuguese Water Dog.

VBO:0201079.summary: Portuguese Water Dog, Shorter And Curly is a variety of Portuguese Water Dog.

VBO:0201080.summary: Docile and devoted to familiar people, the Posavatz Hound is a lively Croatian scent hound with a clear, melodic hunting voice. Its stamina supported hare, fox and boar pursuits and tracking work in the Sava valley; historical depictions and records place red hounds of this type there for centuries.
VBO:0201080.shortDescription: Docile and devoted, this Croatian hound brings stamina and a clear, melodic voice to scent work.
VBO:0201080.historicalRoots: An old red-wheaten scent hound of Croatia’s Sava valley, with related hounds depicted and recorded over several centuries.

VBO:0201082.summary: Posavina Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201083.summary: Potsdam Greyhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201084.summary: Prague Ratters are often gentle and affectionate with familiar people, curious about their surroundings and a little reserved with strangers. Their lively quickness recalls an earlier role catching rats, while their history also reaches the courts of Bohemian rulers.
VBO:0201084.shortDescription: Gentle with familiar people but curious and quick, the Prague Ratter retains an old instinct for catching rats.
VBO:0201084.historicalRoots: Czech rat-catching and royal-court companion history

VBO:0201085.summary: Steady and self-assured, the Presa Canario is attentive to its surroundings and can be reserved with strangers. It developed on Tenerife and Gran Canaria, where historical records describe its work guarding and handling cattle; a deep bark and vigilant stance suit that role.
VBO:0201085.shortDescription: Self-assured and attentive, the Presa Canario has a long tradition of guarding and handling cattle.
VBO:0201085.historicalRoots: Canary Islands molossoid developed chiefly on Tenerife and Gran Canaria for cattle protection.

VBO:0201086.summary: Pshdar Dog is a dog breed or regional type associated with Kurdistan.

VBO:0201087.summary: Calm and self-controlled between tasks, the Pudelpointer carries a strong hunting instinct into field, forest, and water. German breeders founded it from Poodle and Pointer stock to make a versatile pointing gun dog. Its breadth of terrain and steady manner together explain the purpose of that deliberate cross.
VBO:0201087.shortDescription: Calm between tasks, the Pudelpointer searches, points, and retrieves across field, forest, and water.
VBO:0201087.historicalRoots: German versatile gundog from Poodle and Pointer stock.

VBO:0201088.summary: Puerto Rican Mastiff is a dog breed or regional type associated with Puerto Rico.

VBO:0201089.summary: The Pug tends to be lively, happy and even-tempered, with a sociable manner that suited close companionship. Its story runs from China to Europe through Dutch trade, where it became a symbol for royalist supporters in the Netherlands. That court association placed the breed at the center of a very different kind of public life.
VBO:0201089.shortDescription: Lively, happy, and even-tempered, the Pug has long thrived in close companionship, from China to European courts.
VBO:0201089.historicalRoots: Chinese companion dog spread to Europe through Dutch trade.

VBO:0201090.summary: Pug-Labrador Retriever Mix is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0201092.summary: Pug, Apricot is a variety of Pug.

VBO:0201093.summary: Pug, Black is a variety of Pug.

VBO:0201094.summary: Pug, Fawn is a variety of Pug.

VBO:0201095.summary: Pug, Silver is a variety of Pug.

VBO:0201102.summary: Pulis tend to be lively, quick-learning dogs with a watchful streak. Their Hungarian sheep-herding heritage is still central to their identity, and their readiness to learn has carried over into dog sports. The breed’s early history is traditionally linked to the livestock-keeping Magyars who migrated into the Carpathian Basin.
VBO:0201102.shortDescription: Lively and quick to learn, the Puli carries a watchful streak from its Hungarian sheep-herding past.
VBO:0201102.historicalRoots: Hungarian herding dog used around sheep.

registryGroups.label: Group 1 · Sheepdogs and Cattledogs (except Swiss Cattledogs)

VBO:0201103.summary: Puli, Black, Black Shaded With Rust-Red Or Grey, Fawn, Grey In Any Shade is a variety of Puli.

VBO:0201104.summary: Puli, Pearl-White is a variety of Puli.

VBO:0201105.summary: The Pumi is typically bold, busy and vocal, with some reserve toward strangers. Hungarian herders used it to turn larger livestock and sound an alarm around the farm; its early lines combined Puli-type dogs with imported terrier-like herders, helping explain its lively working style.
VBO:0201105.shortDescription: Bold, busy, and vocal, the Pumi turned Hungarian livestock and sounded an alarm around the farm.
VBO:0201105.historicalRoots: Hungarian herder shaped from Puli and continental terrier types.

VBO:0201106.summary: Pumi, Black is a variety of Pumi.

VBO:0201107.summary: Pumi, Fawn (Fakó). Primary Colours: Red, Yellow, Cream is a variety of Pumi.

VBO:0201108.summary: Pumi, Grey In Various Shades is a variety of Pumi.

VBO:0201109.summary: Cooperative group hunting is a documented skill of Pungsan Dogs in Korea’s northern mountains. A university account describes several dogs surrounding large quarry and using barking to hold it in place until a hunter arrives. That coordinated behavior gives the breed a distinctive working tradition in difficult mountain country.
VBO:0201109.shortDescription: In one documented hunting tradition, groups of Pungsan Dogs surround large quarry and bark to hold it for a hunter.

VBO:0201110.summary: Purebred Cross Canine is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0201114.summary: Pyrenean Sheepdog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201115.summary: Pyrenean Sheepdog - Long Haired is a variety of Pyrenean Sheepdog associated with France.

VBO:0201116.summary: Smooth-faced Pyrenean Sheepdogs are lively and responsive, though some remain wary of strangers. In the Pyrenean foothills, horse dealers and cattle drovers valued this working variety; its separate identity was recognized in the breed standard by the 1920s. The shorter hair around the face makes its quick, attentive expression easy to see.
VBO:0201116.shortDescription: Lively and responsive, this smooth-faced Pyrenean worker was valued by cattle drovers in the foothills.
VBO:0201116.historicalRoots: Smooth-faced Pyrenean sheepdog variety long used in foothill livestock movement; described separately by the 1920s.

VBO:0201117.summary: Pyrenean Shepherd is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0201118.summary: Pyrénées Braque Français is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201119.summary: Rache is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201120.summary: Rafeiros do Alentejo are calm, confident guardians traditionally entrusted with both livestock and rural estates. Often most vigilant at night, they accompanied seasonal flock movements from mountain pasture to the Alentejo plains.
VBO:0201120.shortDescription: A calm Alentejo guardian of flocks and estates, especially vigilant at night along the old transhumance routes.

VBO:0201121.summary: Raibs Suns is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201122.summary: The Rajapalayam comes from the area around its namesake town in southern Tamil Nadu. Local households have mainly kept these dogs to guard farms and farmhouses, where watching familiar ground and responding to unfamiliar activity are practical daily jobs; their history is closely tied to that farming region.
VBO:0201122.shortDescription: Around Rajapalayam, local households kept these dogs to watch farms and respond to unfamiliar activity.
VBO:0201122.historicalRoots: Rajapalayam district, Tamil Nadu indigenous working dog.

VBO:0201123.summary: Rampur Greyhound is a dog breed or regional type associated with India.

VBO:0201125.summary: Curious and quick to learn, Rat Terriers can switch from friendly company to fearless, energetic hunting. American farmers prized their speed and persistence against rats and other small vermin. The breed’s sharp attention links that practical farm role with its lively household manner.
VBO:0201125.shortDescription: Curious and quick to learn, the Rat Terrier can turn from friendly company to fearless pursuit of farm vermin.

VBO:0201126.summary: Ratonero Bodeguero Andaluz dogs are curious, cheerful and bold, shaped by close work hunting rodents around Jerez wine cellars and stables. British wine traders brought Smooth Fox Terrier lines to the area, where they blended with local dogs. Their mainly white coat made them easier to spot in dim work spaces, while the breed also retained a nimble, affectionate character.
VBO:0201126.shortDescription: Curious and bold, this Andalusian cellar dog hunted rodents around Jerez wine stores and stables.
VBO:0201126.historicalRoots: Andalusian ratter of Jerez cellars and stables, with local and Smooth Fox Terrier roots.

VBO:0201128.summary: Ratonero Murciano is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201129.summary: Ratonero Valenciano is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201130.summary: Ratter is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201132.summary: The Redbone Coonhound tends to be even-tempered and affectionate, with a strong wish to please and a natural instinct to tree game. It follows raccoon scent over varied terrain and signals when quarry is treed; it can also work in water. Georgia breeder George F. L. Birdsong supplied important foundation stock to the line.
VBO:0201132.shortDescription: Even-tempered and affectionate, the Redbone follows raccoon scent and signals when quarry is treed.
VBO:0201132.historicalRoots: U.S. raccoon-trailing and treeing hound with Georgia foundation lines.

VBO:0201134.summary: Retriever is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201135.summary: Rhodesian Ridgebacks tend to be composed and self-possessed, with a reserved approach to unfamiliar people. Their hunting history involved tracking game in small groups and keeping it at bay until a hunter arrived. The famous “lion dog” story refers to that demanding tracking and holding work, which relied on the dogs’ agility.
VBO:0201135.shortDescription: Composed and reserved with strangers, the Ridgeback historically tracked game in small groups and held it until a hunter arrived.
VBO:0201135.historicalRoots: Southern African multipurpose hound developed from imported and local ridged dogs.

registryGroups.label: Group 6 · Scent hounds and related breeds

VBO:0201137.summary: The Lagotto Romagnolo is generally tractable, affectionate and keen to follow scent. It once retrieved birds from Romagna's marshes, but wetland drainage redirected its nose toward truffles hidden underground; that unusual change of quarry is one of the breed's most memorable skills.
VBO:0201137.shortDescription: Affectionate and keen to follow scent, the Lagotto shifted from marsh bird retrieval to finding underground truffles.
VBO:0201137.historicalRoots: Romagna marsh retriever turned truffle-searching dog.

VBO:0201138.summary: Roman Rottweiler is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201139.summary: Romanian Bucovina Shepherds are calm, loyal flock guardians with a strong low bark used when strangers or predators approach. They traditionally patrol flock or home after dark, a working habit rooted in the transhumance country of northeastern Romania.
VBO:0201139.shortDescription: A calm Bucovina guardian known for low, powerful warning barks and nighttime patrols around flock or home.

VBO:0201140.summary: Romanian Carpathian Shepherd Dogs are calm, stable guardians with a strong attachment to the flock and shepherd. Selected for centuries for protection in the Carpathian mountains, they retain the agile, powerful build needed to patrol rugged grazing ground.
VBO:0201140.shortDescription: A calm, stable Carpathian flock guardian with strong attachment to its herd and the shepherd who tends it.

VBO:0201141.summary: Calm and stable with familiar people, the Romanian Mioritic Shepherd Dog can show striking courage when a flock is threatened. It guarded livestock in the Carpathians against wolves, bears, and lynx while remaining wary of strangers near its charges. Long hours of mountain watch shaped its blend of composure and resolve.
VBO:0201141.shortDescription: Calm with familiar people, the Mioritic Shepherd shows courage when guarding Carpathian flocks from predators.

VBO:0201142.summary: Romanian Raven Shepherd Dogs tend to be calm and attached to their own people, while reserved with strangers. In the southern Carpathians they guarded flocks and households, and their deep bark could carry over a great distance. The breed's name comes from its predominantly black coat.
VBO:0201142.shortDescription: Calm with its own people and reserved with strangers, this Carpathian flock guardian has a far-carrying bark.
VBO:0201142.historicalRoots: Southern Carpathian and sub-Carpathian flock and household guardian of Romania.

VBO:0201143.summary: The Rottweiler tends to be self-assured, steady and eager to work, staying alert without losing an even temper. Its working story runs through cattle driving, guarding and pulling loads in the German town of Rottweil. Butchers favored the breed for usefulness, and police service later drew on the same combination of nerve and willingness.
VBO:0201143.shortDescription: Self-assured and eager to work, the Rottweiler moved cattle, guarded, and pulled loads around Rottweil.
VBO:0201143.interestingFact: The old working name was “Rottweil butcher’s dog.”
VBO:0201143.historicalRoots: German cattle drover and guard dog associated with Rottweil.

VBO:0201144.summary: Rough Beagle is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201145.summary: Russell Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201147.summary: Russian Bolonka is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201148.summary: Russian Harlequin Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201149.summary: Russian Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with Russia.

VBO:0201150.summary: Russian Spaniels tend to be friendly with people, energetic in the field and responsive to a handler. Developed for bird hunting, they search cover, flush game and retrieve it across varied terrain; their work calls for close cooperation as well as the stamina to keep moving.
VBO:0201150.shortDescription: Friendly and energetic, this bird dog works close to its handler to search, flush and retrieve game.
VBO:0201150.historicalRoots: Russian sporting spaniel developed to search, flush and retrieve birds across varied terrain.

VBO:0201151.summary: Russian Toys are often cheerful, curious companions that keep a close eye on their people. When toy-terrier numbers dwindled in Russia, local breeders revived a distinct line in the 1950s. A longhaired pup born to smooth-coated parents in 1958 helped establish the second coat variety of this devoted little dog.
VBO:0201151.shortDescription: Cheerful and curious, the Russian Toy keeps close watch on its people and carries a revived Russian companion lineage.
VBO:0201151.historicalRoots: Russian companion dog revived from local toy-terrier stock in the mid-1950s.

VBO:0201152.summary: Russian Toy, Longhaired is a variety of Russian Toy.

VBO:0201153.summary: Russian Toy, Smooth-Haired is a variety of Russian Toy.

VBO:0201154.summary: Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka is a variety of Russian Bolonka associated with Russia.

VBO:0201155.summary: Russian-European Laikas are steady, even-tempered hunting dogs with a keen nose for detecting game. They come from the forest regions of European Russia, where regional Laika populations were brought under a single breed name in 1947. The purebred standard was approved in 1952, after a longer process of selective breeding.
VBO:0201155.shortDescription: Even-tempered and keen-nosed, this Russian forest hunter was consolidated from regional Laika lines after World War II.

VBO:0201156.summary: Ryukyu Inu is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201158.summary: Saarloos Wolfhonden are lively, independent dogs whose devotion to familiar people can sit beside reserve with strangers and a preference to avoid unfamiliar situations. Leendert Saarloos developed the breed from a German Shepherd–wolf cross; although he sought a working dog, the resulting breed became known for its own distinct character.
VBO:0201158.shortDescription: Devoted to familiar people yet inclined to retreat from unfamiliar situations, this wolfdog has a strong independent streak.

VBO:0201159.summary: Sage is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201160.summary: Saint Bernards are generally friendly and watchful, with individuals ranging from calm to lively. At the Great St Bernard Pass, monks kept them as guards and used them to find travelers lost in snow or fog; the famous rescue role grew from the daily needs of an actual mountain hospice.
VBO:0201160.shortDescription: Friendly and watchful, Saint Bernards once found travelers lost in snow or fog near a mountain hospice.
VBO:0201160.historicalRoots: Great St. Bernard Pass hospice and alpine rescue dog.

VBO:0201161.summary: Saint Bernard, Long-Haired is a variety of Saint Bernard.

VBO:0201162.summary: Saint Bernard, Short-Haired is a variety of Saint Bernard.

VBO:0201163.summary: Saint Germain Pointer is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0201164.summary: Saint Hubert Bloodhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201165.summary: Saint Hubert Jura Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201166.summary: Saint John's Water Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201167.summary: Saint Miguel Cattle Dogs are determined drovers and attentive guardians from São Miguel in the Azores, receptive to their owners yet wary of strangers. When driving dairy cattle, they have a distinctive working habit: nipping low to avoid injuring the udder.
VBO:0201167.shortDescription: An Azorean cattle drover, this determined dog works carefully with dairy herds and stays responsive to its owner.

VBO:0201168.summary: Saint-Usuge Spaniel is a dog breed or regional type associated with France.

VBO:0201169.summary: Sakhalin Husky is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201170.summary: Salish Wool Dog is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201171.summary: Salukis tend to be independent and dignified, often greeting strangers with reserve. They come from a long Middle Eastern tradition of hunting by sight, with local dogs valued for pursuing the game found in their own region. In Middle Eastern tradition, Salukis were presented as marks of honor.
VBO:0201171.shortDescription: Independent and dignified, the Saluki often greets strangers with reserve and comes from Middle Eastern sight hunting.
VBO:0201171.historicalRoots: Ancient Middle Eastern sighthound tradition spanning multiple regions and local types.

VBO:0201172.summary: Saluki, Fringed is a variety of Saluki.

VBO:0201173.summary: Saluki, Smooth is a variety of Saluki.

VBO:0201174.summary: Open, lively, and sociable with people, Samoyeds grew from a long partnership with northern Russian and Siberian communities. They helped with herding, hunting, and sledge travel, sometimes sharing shelter with the people beside whom they worked.
VBO:0201174.shortDescription: Lively and sociable, Samoyeds worked beside northern communities in herding, hunting, and sledge travel.
VBO:0201174.historicalRoots: Northern Russian and Siberian sled and reindeer work.

VBO:0201175.summary: Sanshu Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201176.summary: Sapsali is a dog breed or regional type associated with South Korea.

VBO:0201177.summary: Sapsari is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201178.summary: Sarabi Dog is a dog breed or regional type associated with Iran.

VBO:0201179.summary: Sardinian Shepherd Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201180.summary: The Šarplaninac tends to be reliable, protective and devoted to its handler, with an even disposition rather than a quick, indiscriminate reaction. It guarded cattle herds against predators in the mountain region that gave the breed its name. The role continues an old Balkan livestock-guardian tradition.
VBO:0201180.shortDescription: Reliable and protective, the Šarplaninac guarded Balkan cattle herds with an even, considered response to threats.
VBO:0201180.historicalRoots: Balkan livestock guardian of the Šar mountain region.

VBO:0201181.summary: Lively, cheerful and watchful, the Schapendoes brings an independent mind to sheep work. On Dutch heathlands it needed quick turns, jumping ability and stamina to manage flocks; after nearly disappearing during the Second World War, the breed was rebuilt by dedicated keepers.
VBO:0201181.shortDescription: Cheerful and watchful, the Schapendoes brings quick turns and an independent mind to Dutch sheep work.

VBO:0201182.summary: Schiller Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with Sweden.

VBO:0201184.summary: Alert and curious, Schipperkes tend to investigate closed doors, moving objects, and unfamiliar visitors, often sounding a sharp alarm. They grew from Flemish working communities as small guardians. Their name means “little shepherd,” a clue to roots deeper than the canal-barge story often attached to them.
VBO:0201184.shortDescription: Curious and alert, the Schipperke investigates closed doors and unfamiliar visitors, often giving a sharp alarm.

VBO:0201185.summary: The Schnauzer is typically playful and devoted with familiar people, alert to intruders yet not expected to bark without pause. It began as a southern German stable dog, keeping company with horses and dispatching rodents around the yard. The early nickname “Rattler” captures the practical job beneath today’s companion role.
VBO:0201185.shortDescription: Playful with familiar people and alert to intruders, the Schnauzer once kept stables free of rodents.
VBO:0201185.historicalRoots: Southern German stable and rodent-control dog.

VBO:0201186.summary: Schnauzer-Beagle Cross is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0201187.summary: Schnauzer, Pepper And Salt is a variety of Schnauzer.

VBO:0201188.summary: Schnauzer, Pure Black With Black Undercoat is a variety of Schnauzer.

VBO:0201189.summary: Schnauzer, Standard is a variety of Schnauzer associated with Germany.

VBO:0201195.summary: The Scottish Deerhound is commonly gentle, friendly and dignified, with an eagerness to please that contrasts with its formidable chase. It was bred to course red deer across open Scottish country, a pursuit demanding speed and persistence; the partnership reaches back many centuries.
VBO:0201195.shortDescription: Gentle and dignified in company, the Scottish Deerhound brings speed and persistence to red-deer coursing.

VBO:0201196.summary: Scottish Rough Collie is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201197.summary: Scottish Smooth Collie is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201198.summary: Loyal yet independent, the Scottish Terrier often meets the world with dignified reserve. Highland breeders valued the courage and intelligence needed to investigate quarry underground and keep working in difficult terrain.
VBO:0201198.shortDescription: Loyal but independent, the Scottish Terrier meets the world with reserve and persists when exploring quarry underground.

VBO:0201199.summary: Sealydale Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201200.summary: The Sealyham Terrier tends to be game and fearless on the job but friendly in ordinary company. It was developed in Wales for hard terrier work alongside otterhounds and against vermin. Captain John Edwardes shaped the strain at his Sealy Ham estate, giving the dog both its name and a very specific working origin.
VBO:0201200.shortDescription: Fearless at work but friendly in company, the Sealyham Terrier was shaped for hard Welsh vermin and otter work.
VBO:0201200.historicalRoots: Welsh earth-working terrier later kept as a companion.

VBO:0201201.summary: The Segugio dell'Appennino has a strong hunting drive and can work closely with its handler while showing initiative on the trail. Bred for hare country in the Apennines, these hounds search and follow scent across steep ground, sometimes alone and sometimes in pairs.
VBO:0201201.shortDescription: Driven to follow hare scent through Apennine hills, this hound works alone or in a pair with its handler.
VBO:0201201.historicalRoots: Italian Apennine hare-hunting hound used on mountainous ground.

VBO:0201202.summary: Segugio Italiano is a dog breed or regional type associated with Italy.

VBO:0201203.summary: Self-confident and driven in the field, the Segugio Maremmano was shaped by Tuscan boar hunters for work in the Maremma landscape. Its voice changes with phases of the hunt, and it can pursue quarry alone or in a pack; the breed also works hare and other mammals.
VBO:0201203.shortDescription: Self-confident in the field, this Tuscan hound uses a changing voice to mark phases of the hunt.
VBO:0201203.historicalRoots: Developed from local hunting dogs in southern Tuscany’s Maremma for wild boar work, with formal breed efforts since the 1930s.

VBO:0201204.summary: Serbian Balkan Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201207.summary: Lively and kind-natured, the Serbian Hound can become tenacious when it finds a trail. This Balkan scent hunter uses stamina and a clear voice to keep the chase moving; once called the Balkan Hound, it took its present name as the regional hunting tradition became more closely tied to Serbia.
VBO:0201207.shortDescription: Lively and kind-natured, the Serbian Hound grows tenacious on a scent trail, using a clear voice through the chase.

VBO:0201208.summary: Serbian Mountain Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201209.summary: Serbian Tricolor Hounds are devoted and lively companions with the tenacity to keep following a scent. Their independent standing as a breed was settled in 1946, after a period when they were treated as a variety of the Serbian Hound; international recognition followed in 1961.
VBO:0201209.shortDescription: Kind and lively yet persistent on a scent, this Balkan hound was recognized apart from the Serbian Hound.
VBO:0201209.historicalRoots: Balkan tricolored scent hound recognized as distinct from the Serbian Hound in 1946.

VBO:0201210.summary: Serrano Bulldog is a dog breed or regional type associated with Brazil.

VBO:0201211.summary: Setter is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201215.summary: Sheepdog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201216.summary: Shepherd Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201217.summary: Alert and responsive with familiar people, Shetland Sheepdogs can be more reserved on first meeting strangers. Their quick learning and attention to movement grew from island sheep work, even as the breed became a close companion. That persistent working focus remains one of their less visible qualities.
VBO:0201217.shortDescription: Responsive with familiar people but reserved at first with strangers, the Sheltie keeps close watch on movement from island sheep work.

VBO:0201218.summary: Shi-Jug is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201220.summary: Shiba Inus are keenly alert and attentive to their surroundings, with a strong sense of attachment to familiar people. Their roots lie in hunting birds and small animals in Japan’s mountain country. When local strains became scarce after widespread crossing with imported hunting dogs, Japanese hunters helped organize the effort to preserve them.
VBO:0201220.shortDescription: Keenly alert and attached to familiar people, the Shiba Inu carries a hunting heritage from Japan’s mountain country.
VBO:0201220.historicalRoots: Japanese native hunting spitz associated with mountainous regions.

VBO:0201223.summary: The Shih Tzu tends to be friendly, alert and independent, carrying a self-possessed manner into close companionship. It has Tibetan roots but grew into a favored companion in Chinese imperial palaces before spreading west. British imports in the 1930s helped establish the modern Western population.
VBO:0201223.shortDescription: Friendly and independent, the Shih Tzu brings a self-possessed manner to a long history of palace companionship.
VBO:0201223.historicalRoots: Tibetan roots and Chinese palace development as a companion dog.

VBO:0201225.summary: Keen, energetic and highly alert, the Shikoku was shaped by boar hunting in Japan's Kochi mountains. It remains responsive to its handler while pursuing game over steep terrain; the old Awa, Hongawa and Hata lines preserve the breed's connection to different local hunting communities.
VBO:0201225.shortDescription: Keen and energetic, the Shikoku responds to its handler while pursuing boar across steep Kochi mountain ground.

VBO:0201226.summary: Shiloh Shepherd is a dog breed or regional type associated with United States.

VBO:0201231.summary: Shropshire Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201233.summary: Outgoing and gentle with people, Siberian Huskies often lack the suspicion expected of a guard dog. Their historic skill was teamwork in harness, moving light loads at a steady pace over great distances. Endurance and efficient cooperation, rather than guarding, define their working past.
VBO:0201233.shortDescription: Outgoing and gentle with people, the Siberian Husky thrives in cooperative harness work over long distances.

VBO:0201234.summary: Sicillian Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201235.summary: Gentle and affectionate at home, Silken Windhounds retain the keen prey drive of a field sighthound. This modern American breed was developed from Borzoi and Whippet lines to bring a smaller, long-coated hound into the family of sporting sight hunters, while keeping its fine-boned grace and speed.
VBO:0201235.shortDescription: Gentle and devoted at home, this silky American sighthound keeps a keen eye for moving prey in the field.
VBO:0201235.historicalRoots: A modern American sighthound developed using Borzoi and Whippet lines for a smaller, long-coated sporting dog.

VBO:0201236.summary: Silky Spitz is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201237.summary: The Silky Terrier tends to be active, keenly alert and courageous, ready to investigate movement with the quick response of a terrier. It emerged in Australia from local terrier and Yorkshire lines and became a close companion without losing that inquisitive spirit. Early breeders shaped the type around Sydney before it spread more widely.
VBO:0201237.shortDescription: Active and courageous, the Silky Terrier investigates movement quickly, carrying Australian terrier instincts into companionship.
VBO:0201237.historicalRoots: Australian companion terrier shaped from local and Yorkshire lines.

VBO:0201238.summary: Simaku is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201239.summary: Sinhala Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201240.summary: The Skye Terrier often forms a strong bond with one person and may be reserved when strangers first approach. Its ancestors pursued quarry among the rocks and earth of Scotland's western islands; Greyfriars Bobby's famous vigil became a lasting story of the breed's devotion.
VBO:0201240.shortDescription: Closely bonded with its person and sometimes reserved with strangers, the Skye Terrier once pursued quarry among island rocks.

VBO:0201241.summary: Sleuth Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201242.summary: Strongly attached to their own people, Sloughis can also respond protectively when those people are threatened. Across North Africa they pursued game over open ground, drawing on keen chase instinct and sustained effort. Away from that work, this dignified sighthound is also noted for enjoying the comforts of home.
VBO:0201242.shortDescription: Attached to its own people and dignified at home, the Sloughi brings a keen chase instinct to North African open ground.

VBO:0201244.summary: Slovakian Wire-Haired Pointer is a dog breed or regional type associated with Slovakia.

VBO:0201245.summary: Slovensky Cuvacs are vigilant and courageous, with a strong attachment to the people and flocks they guard. For centuries they worked on high Slovak mountain pastures, watching livestock through harsh weather and sounding the alarm when danger approached. Their white coat helped shepherds distinguish them from predators after dark; the breed’s name also echoes its keen watchfulness.
VBO:0201245.shortDescription: Vigilant and brave, this white Slovak mountain guardian watches flocks and stays closely attached to its people.
VBO:0201245.historicalRoots: Slovak Tatra mountain guardian of livestock and pasture camps.

VBO:0201246.summary: Slovensky Kopovs are spirited scent hounds known for keeping their direction while following a warm trail. In Slovakia they can work a track for hours, giving tongue as they pursue wild boar. Their compact, lightly built frame supports the sustained movement this work demands.
VBO:0201246.shortDescription: Spirited and sure of direction, this Slovak hound follows a warm trail for hours and gives tongue on boar hunts.
VBO:0201246.historicalRoots: Slovak black-and-tan scent hound used to follow warm boar trails for hours while giving tongue.

VBO:0201247.summary: Smaland Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with Sweden.

VBO:0201250.summary: Small Munsterlander is a dog breed or regional type associated with Germany.

VBO:0201251.summary: Small Swiss Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with Switzerland.

VBO:0201252.summary: Small Swiss Hound, Small Bernese Hound is a variety of Small Swiss Hound.

VBO:0201253.summary: Small Swiss Hound, Small Jura Hound is a variety of Small Swiss Hound.

VBO:0201254.summary: Small Swiss Hound, Small Lucerne Hound is a variety of Small Swiss Hound.

VBO:0201255.summary: Small Swiss Hound, Small Schwyz Hound is a variety of Small Swiss Hound.

VBO:0201256.summary: Smithfield is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201257.summary: Smooth Beagle is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201258.summary: Smooth Fox Terriers are lively, sociable and quick to meet a new challenge. Britain’s foxhunts shaped a dog ready to pursue foxes, and the old working brief also included rats and rabbits. Their bright, expectant manner hints at a terrier that was bred to move fast and keep its attention on the task.
VBO:0201258.shortDescription: Lively and sociable, the Smooth Fox Terrier reacts quickly to a challenge, reflecting fox, rat, and rabbit work.
VBO:0201258.historicalRoots: British foxhunting terrier standardized by the late 19th century.

VBO:0201260.summary: Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier is a variety of Wheaten Terrier.

VBO:0201261.summary: Soft-Coated Wheaten, English American Terrier is a variety of Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.

VBO:0201262.summary: Soft-Coated Wheaten, Heavy Irish Terrier is a variety of Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.

VBO:0201263.summary: Soft-Coated Wheaten, Traditional Irish Terrier is a variety of Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier.

VBO:0201264.summary: South Russian Shepherd Dogs tend to be self-confident and independent, strongly devoted to their people but reserved with strangers. Their long shaggy coat can hide an agile worker: they guarded cattle and property across open southern steppe country. The breed took its modern name and formal shape in the early twentieth century after earlier bearded herding dogs mixed with local stock.
VBO:0201264.shortDescription: Self-confident and devoted to its people, this shaggy steppe guardian remains reserved with strangers.
VBO:0201264.historicalRoots: Southern Russian steppe herding and guardian breed, standardized in the early twentieth century.

VBO:0201265.summary: South Russian Steppe Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201267.summary: Southern Blackmouth Cur is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201268.summary: Southern Bloodhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201270.summary: Southern Hound is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201271.summary: Spaniel is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201275.summary: Spanish Hounds are affectionate and calm off the hunt, yet notably brave when following larger game. Hunters listen to changes in the hound's voice to tell whether it has found an old line, a fresh one or the end of a chase. The Sabueso also has a long reputation for hare work, recorded in Spanish hunting writing since the late Middle Ages.
VBO:0201275.shortDescription: Calm and affectionate off the hunt, this Spanish hound changes its voice as a scent trail develops.
VBO:0201275.historicalRoots: Sabueso Español documented in late-medieval Spanish hunting texts; specialist in hare and blood tracking.

VBO:0201276.summary: Spanish Hound, Large is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201277.summary: Spanish Hound, Small is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201278.summary: The Spanish Mastiff tends to pair affection toward familiar people with resolve when stock or property is threatened. It traveled with Merino flocks on seasonal routes, staying close enough to defend animals from wolves in changing pastures. Its story is inseparable from Spain’s old transhumant sheep culture and the medieval Mesta.
VBO:0201278.shortDescription: Affectionate with familiar people yet resolute on guard, the Spanish Mastiff defended Merino flocks on seasonal routes.
VBO:0201278.historicalRoots: Spanish transhumant flock guardian, especially with Merino sheep.

VBO:0201280.summary: Spanish Water Dogs tend to be lively, watchful and quick to grasp a task, with a strong willingness to work alongside people. Their traditional jobs ranged across herding, hunting and assisting fishermen. Readiness to learn and adapt to changing conditions was useful across that varied working life.
VBO:0201280.shortDescription: Lively and watchful, the Spanish Water Dog learned varied work beside people, from herding to fishing and hunting.
VBO:0201280.historicalRoots: Spanish multipurpose working dog used for herding and water-related tasks.

VBO:0201282.summary: Spitz is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201284.summary: Sporting Lucas Terrier is a dog breed or regional type associated with Scotland.

VBO:0201287.summary: Springer Spaniel is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201289.summary: Sprocker Spaniel is a named crossbreed.

VBO:0201293.summary: Stabijhouns often combine affection with an independent streak; at home they can be quiet and watchful, while unfamiliar people may meet a reserved first response. Their Frisian farm history is unusually varied: they pointed game, guarded yards and caught moles and polecats, with smaller dogs once carried by bicycle to reach more trapping ground.
VBO:0201293.shortDescription: Affectionate but independent, the Stabijhoun pointed game, guarded Frisian yards, and caught moles and polecats.
VBO:0201293.historicalRoots: Versatile pointing and farm dog from the Frisian forest area of the Netherlands.

VBO:0201296.summary: Staffordshire Bull Terriers tend to be affectionate and playful with familiar people, bringing a warm social manner to everyday life. They also retain the courage and tenacity of their terrier ancestry; an intelligent, watchful dog can shift from play to focused attention when something around it changes.
VBO:0201296.shortDescription: Playful and affectionate with familiar people, the Staffordshire Bull Terrier retains terrier courage and watchfulness.

VBO:0201297.summary: Staffordshire Bull Terrier, English is a variety of Staffordshire Bull Terrier.

VBO:0201298.summary: Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Irish is a variety of Staffordshire Bull Terrier.

VBO:0201299.summary: Staffordshire Bull Terrier, Miniature is a variety of Staffordshire Bull Terrier.

VBO:0201300.summary: Staghound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201302.summary: Stephens' Cur is a dog breed or regional type associated with United States.

VBO:0201305.summary: Tough and determined on a track, the Styrian Coarse-Haired Hound was developed for mountain hunting and wounded-game tracking. The breed traces to an 1870 cross arranged by Carl Peintinger in Styria; its rough weather-ready coat supports a hound known for giving tongue while working difficult terrain.
VBO:0201305.shortDescription: Tough and determined on mountain tracks, this Styrian hound gives tongue as it follows game.
VBO:0201305.historicalRoots: Developed in Styria from an 1870 Hanoverian Scent Hound–coarse-haired Istrian Hound cross selected for mountain work.

VBO:0201306.summary: Styrian Rough-Haired Mountain Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201307.summary: Styrian Wire-Haired Mountain Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201308.summary: Sussex Bulldog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201309.summary: Kindly in manner yet persistent on a scent, the Sussex Spaniel has a useful habit of giving voice while working thick cover. That call helps a hunter follow progress after the dog disappears into vegetation. The combination of steady determination and audible hunting sets it apart from quieter spaniels.
VBO:0201309.shortDescription: Kindly yet persistent on a scent, the Sussex Spaniel gives voice in thick cover so its hunter can follow.

VBO:0201310.summary: Swedish Briard is a variety of Briard.

VBO:0201311.summary: Swedish Cattle Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201315.summary: The Swedish Lapphund tends to be alert, affectionate and eager to engage with work; endurance and a ready response to training support its varied jobs. Sámi communities used it with reindeer, while northern households also valued it for hunting and watch duties. This range gave the breed a broader working history than herding alone.
VBO:0201315.shortDescription: Alert and affectionate, the Swedish Lapphund worked with Sámi reindeer and also took on hunting and watch duties.
VBO:0201315.historicalRoots: Sámi reindeer-herding, hunting and watch dog of Sweden.

VBO:0201316.summary: Alert, energetic and fearless, the Swedish Vallhund can work close to cattle heels with confidence around much larger animals. The breed survived on farms in West Gothland, where a 1940s search found remaining dogs and helped preserve an old Swedish herding tradition.
VBO:0201316.shortDescription: Alert and fearless, the Swedish Vallhund works close to cattle heels with confidence around much larger animals.

VBO:0201317.summary: Swedish White Elkhound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201318.summary: Swiss Hound is a dog breed or regional type associated with Switzerland.

VBO:0201319.summary: Swiss Hound, Bernese Hound is a variety of Swiss Hound.

VBO:0201320.summary: Swiss Hound, Jura Hound is a variety of Swiss Hound.

VBO:0201321.summary: Swiss Hound, Lucerne Hound is a variety of Swiss Hound.

VBO:0201322.summary: Swiss Hound, Schwyz Hound is a variety of Swiss Hound.

VBO:0201323.summary: Swiss Mountain Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201324.summary: Swiss Short-Haired Pinscher is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201325.summary: Swiss White Shepherd Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201327.summary: Sydney Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201328.summary: Tahitian Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201329.summary: Tahltan is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201331.summary: Persistent across broken highland ground, the Taigan can join coordinated Kyrgyz hunts with a golden eagle. National kennel accounts describe pursuit of fox, ibex, and other game at elevations that challenge many coursing dogs. Mountain stamina and that unusual partnership give the breed a distinct working story.
VBO:0201331.shortDescription: Persistent on highland hunts, the Taigan can pursue game alongside a Kyrgyz golden eagle.

VBO:0201333.summary: Talbot Hound is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201334.summary: Tamaskan Dogs are generally friendly and outgoing, although some meet new people with a little reserve and can work independently. Their northern sled-dog heritage shows in an active, willing worker able to pull light loads at a moderate pace over short distances.
VBO:0201334.shortDescription: Friendly and willing to work, this northern sled-dog descendant may be reserved at first.
VBO:0201334.historicalRoots: Modern northern sled-dog-derived breed represented by the Tamaskan Dog Register.

VBO:0201335.summary: Tamaskan Husky is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201338.summary: Tazy dogs are calm and self-possessed in ordinary life, then swift and keen when hunting. On Kazakhstan’s open land they have worked alone, in groups and alongside hunting birds, using both sight and scent to search for game. The breed appears in Kazakh tradition as one of the Seven Treasures, a reminder of its long connection to nomadic hunting life.
VBO:0201338.shortDescription: Calm at rest and keen in the field, the Tazy hunts across Kazakhstan’s open country with sight and scent.
VBO:0201338.historicalRoots: Kazakh sighthound of nomadic hunting culture, used alone, in groups and with hunting birds.

VBO:0201339.summary: Teacup Pomeranian is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201340.summary: Lively, alert and affectionate, the Teddy Roosevelt Terrier has a strong ratting and farm-work inheritance. The low-set, short-legged terrier is curious and often eager to join familiar people’s activities; historically it was known as the Type B or bench-legged Rat Terrier before adopting its present name.
VBO:0201340.shortDescription: Lively, affectionate and curious, this short-legged farm terrier has a long tradition of ratting work.
VBO:0201340.historicalRoots: An American short-legged ratting and farm terrier related to the Rat Terrier and formerly known as the Type B or bench-legged Rat Terrier.

VBO:0201341.summary: Telomian is a dog breed or regional type associated with Malaysia.

VBO:0201342.summary: The Tenterfield Terrier tends to be quick, agile and alert, traits once put to work against vermin around Australian farms. Small ratting terriers arrived with English settlers and became a distinct local type; later dogs also took part in tracking and earthdog sports. Its inquisitive nature links the old pest-control job to those newer activities.
VBO:0201342.shortDescription: Quick and inquisitive, the Tenterfield Terrier took on Australian farm vermin and later tracking and earthdog work.
VBO:0201342.interestingFact: The name honors Tenterfield saddler George Woolnough, whose terriers were known in the district.
VBO:0201342.historicalRoots: Australian farm and homestead vermin-control terrier.

VBO:0201343.summary: Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201346.summary: Tesem is a historical dog breed or type.

VBO:0201347.summary: The Thai Bangkaew Dog is often alert, intelligent and loyal, with some reserve toward strangers. Its name comes from a village in Phitsanulok, where watchful household dogs developed a local identity; readiness to learn and respond to familiar people complements that guarding instinct.
VBO:0201347.shortDescription: Alert and loyal with familiar people, the Thai Bangkaew Dog carries a watchful household tradition from its namesake village.

VBO:0201348.summary: Thai Ridgebacks are active, resilient dogs with a strong attachment to their families and a remarkable talent for jumping. In eastern Thailand they hunted, kept watch and accompanied carts on journeys. Difficult travel between communities helped preserve the local dogs, giving the breed a history tied to everyday work as well as companionship.
VBO:0201348.shortDescription: Active and strongly attached to its people, the Thai Ridgeback hunted, watched, and traveled with carts in eastern Thailand.
VBO:0201348.historicalRoots: Long-established Thai ridged dog associated with eastern regions of the country.

VBO:0201349.summary: Tiara Teddy Bear is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201350.summary: Tibetan Kyi Apso is a dog breed or regional type associated with Tibet.

VBO:0201351.summary: Protective of territory and closely loyal to familiar people, Tibetan Mastiffs tend to meet unfamiliar activity with serious watchfulness. Their Himalayan history includes guarding herds and monasteries, work that called for patience and independent judgment. The breed matures slowly; males may take four years or more to reach full development.
VBO:0201351.shortDescription: Territorial and loyal to familiar people, the Tibetan Mastiff guards with patience and independent judgment.

VBO:0201352.summary: The Tibetan Spaniel tends to be alert and loyal yet independent, sometimes aloof with strangers. Tibetan Spaniels served as both close companions and sentinels at Tibetan monasteries, watching from high walls and barking when something unusual approached. Its name is misleading: these were not European-style bird-flushing spaniels.
VBO:0201352.shortDescription: Alert and independent, the Tibetan Spaniel watched from monastery walls and barked at unusual arrivals.

VBO:0201353.summary: Lively and good-natured with familiar people, the Tibetan Terrier may be more reserved on a first meeting. It lived with Tibetan families, travelers and herders as a companion and watchful partner; despite the name, it is not a working earth terrier.
VBO:0201353.shortDescription: Lively with familiar people but sometimes reserved at first, the Tibetan Terrier was a companion and watchful travel partner.
VBO:0201353.historicalRoots: Tibetan herding, travel and companion dog.

VBO:0201354.summary: Titan Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201355.summary: Tonya Finosu is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201356.summary: Calm and affectionate with familiar people, Tornjaks can become formidable when guarding entrusted livestock or property. In the mountains of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia, they watched flocks and farmyards while keeping a careful eye on strangers. Modern breeders rebuilt the type from scattered survivors of that older pastoral tradition.
VBO:0201356.shortDescription: Calm and affectionate with familiar people, the Tornjak becomes resolute when guarding mountain flocks and farmyards.
VBO:0201356.interestingFact: Historical documents dated 1067 and 1374 mention dogs associated with the Tornjak’s region.
VBO:0201356.historicalRoots: Bosnian and Croatian mountain livestock protection.

VBO:0201357.summary: Composed and patient, the Tosa is known for quiet boldness. Bred in Japan’s Tosa region from Shikoku-ken and several Western breeds, it emerged from a historical fighting tradition; the FCI now recognizes its watchdog role.
VBO:0201357.shortDescription: Patient and composed yet bold, the Tosa is a Japanese mastiff whose role shifted from fighting to watching.
VBO:0201357.historicalRoots: Japanese molossoid developed in the Tosa region; historically used in dog fighting, now listed by FCI as watchdog.

VBO:0201359.summary: Toy Australian Shepherd Dog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201360.summary: Toy Bulldog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201361.summary: The Toy Fox Terrier tends to be quick and athletic, with an eagerness to learn that once brought some into circus performances. It grew from small Smooth Fox Terriers that proved useful as ratters on American farms. That mix of farm ratting, eager movement and trainable performance makes its history unusually varied.
VBO:0201361.shortDescription: Quick and eager to learn, the Toy Fox Terrier ranged from American farm ratting to circus performances.
VBO:0201361.historicalRoots: American small farm ratter developed from Smooth Fox Terrier stock.

VBO:0201363.summary: Toy Manchester Terrier is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201374.summary: Active, alert and intelligent, the Treeing Walker Coonhound can stay with a raccoon scent deep into a night hunt. It signals from the base of a tree when quarry is located, using its characteristic voice to guide a hunter to the end of a trail that may be out of sight.
VBO:0201374.shortDescription: Active and alert, the Treeing Walker follows raccoon scent through night hunts and voices when quarry is treed.

VBO:0201375.summary: Trigg Hound is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201381.summary: Gos Rater Valencià dogs are lively and affectionate with familiar people, while keeping a watchful reserve around strangers. Valencian farms valued their quick warning bark and their persistence against rats, moles and rabbits. The breed’s rise coincided with orange growing in the region; its small working build let it move through cultivated fields and farm edges.
VBO:0201381.shortDescription: Lively and affectionate with familiar people, this small Valencian farm dog warns quickly and pursues pests.
VBO:0201381.historicalRoots: Valencian farm ratter and alert dog associated with nineteenth-century orange-growing country.

VBO:0201382.summary: Valley Bulldog is a dog breed or regional type.

VBO:0201383.summary: Verelade is a dog breed or regional type.
